items.title: Économie russe : les dépenses publiques se rapprochent de la moyenne de l’OCDE
items.description: Selon Alexandre Isakov, directeur du Centre de recherches macroéconomiques de Sber et économiste en chef de la banque publique de développement Vnesheconombank (VEB), les dépenses du budget consolidé de la Russie représenteraient environ 39 % du PIB, soit un niveau proche de la moyenne des pays membres de l’OCDE (42,6 % en 2023) Александр Исаков — РБК : « Экономика России — в стадии принятия новой себя », RBC , 15 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Isakov note que la part du budget dans le PIB de la Russie a considérablement augmenté ces dernières années. En 2018-2019, soit avant le lancement de l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine, les dépenses du budget consolidé représentaient environ un tiers du PIB (32 à 33 % selon Isakov). Cette part aurait ainsi progressé de plus de 6 points entre 2018 et 2025, alors qu’elle n’a gagné qu’environ 2,4 points pour l’OCDE entre 2018 et 2023. L’écart entre la Russie et les pays de l’OCDE se situe aujourd’hui à 3,3 points (sur la base des chiffres de 2023 pour l’OCDE), contre près de 10 points en 2011. La Russie s’approcherait ainsi de la limite supérieure de la taille du secteur public compatible avec des taux de croissance élevés et durables. Selon Isakov, le franchissement du seuil de 40 % pèserait sur les entreprises, l’investissement et sur la capacité du budget à collecter les impôts. Il estime en effet que les entreprises russes reportent déjà leurs investissements en raison de l’incertitude fiscale et du risque macroéconomique, ce qui réduit la demande et la base fiscale potentielle de l’État. Cette incertitude est alimentée par les hausses d’impôts successives destinées à financer l’augmentation des dépenses publiques : l’impôt sur les bénéfices est passé de 20 à 25 % en 2025, la TVA de 20 à 22 % le 1er janvier 2026. La hausse des dépenses de l’État russe est principalement alimentée par le budget de la défense, qui devrait bondir de 32 % en 2027 pour atteindre 17 100 milliards de roubles (environ 182 milliards d’euros). D’ici la fin de l’année, les dépenses militaires russes pourraient ainsi dépasser les 10 % du PIB pour la première fois depuis l’époque soviétique. Le niveau élevé des dépenses publiques dans les pays de l’OCDE, et notamment dans ceux qui sont également membres de l’Union européenne, où la moyenne atteint 49,2 % du PIB (contre 42,6 % en moyenne dans l’OCDE en 2023 et 39 % en Russie en 2025), s’explique principalement par le poids de la protection sociale. La part du PIB consacrée aux dépenses sociales, à la santé et à l’éducation représente en effet environ 27 % dans les pays de l’OCDE (13,4 % pour la protection sociale, 8,4 % pour la santé et 4,9 % pour l’éducation), et 31 % dans ceux de l’Union européenne, contre 19 % en Russie en 2021, selon nos calculs à partir des données du ministère des Finances. L’article Économie russe : les dépenses publiques se rapprochent de la moyenne de l’OCDE est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Diaz dazzles as Bayern Munich batter Leipzig 6-1 to go top
items.description: Luis Diaz hit a hat-trick as Bayern Munich pummelled a listless RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday to climb to the top of the Bundesliga. Borussia Dortmund had briefly edged ahead of Freiburg into top spot after their earlier draw at Union Berlin, but Bayern responded in typically ruthless fashion. In his 100th Bundesliga match, Harry Kane scored a goal and laid on two assists as he pulled the strings from deep, while Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet. The dominant display was probably Bayern’s best performance of the season and a boost to their confidence ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash with English champions Arsenal. “A big game against one of the best in Europe, you have to enjoy these occasions,” Kane told reporters. “We’re testing ourselves against one of the best.” Diaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life at the Allianz Arena in Munich, terrorising Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left. “Lucho (Diaz) has had some criticism this season but he was excellent tonight. Definitely the man of the hour,” Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich said. Confined to his chair with a hip complaint, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany produced a masterclass against opposite number Martin Demichelis, his former Manchester City teammate. “You can come here and lose a match, but not like that,” Demichelis said to Sky Germany. Leipzig travel to face Real Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday. Bayern have now won their past three games against Leipzig by a combined scoreline of 17-1. This result came after two successive draws, a rare run of middling form for the German giants, but they shook off the funk early on, with Diaz, Pavlovic and Olise putting the hosts in control before half-time. Diaz scored either side of a Kane tap-in after the break, with the England captain and former Tottenham striker withdrawn before the hour mark ahead of old rivals Arsenal’s visit. Leipzig’s Andrija Maksimovic got on the board with a consolation in stoppage time. – Dortmund draw in Berlin – Dortmund missed a chance to stay ahead of Bayern after being held to a scoreless draw at Union Berlin. After starting the season strongly with six wins in a row in all competitions, Dortmund have stalled of late, drawing two and losing one of their last three matches. “We simply have to get better in attack. Right now, it’s just not good enough,” Dortmund’s Waldemar Anton told Sky. Serhou Guirassy had a golden chance to snatch all three points for his side at the end of a match of few opportunities, but headed just wide with 11 minutes remaining. It was the first draw between the two sides in their history, with each of their previous 16 clashes in all competitions producing a winner. Compounding Dortmund’s woes was a serious-looking ankle injury to substitute midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas, who was helped from the pitch just eight minutes after coming on. “Let’s hope it’s not too serious. He’s not feeling great right now,” Dortmund sporting director Nils-Ole Book told reporters. Stuttgart suffered a blow ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, going down 1-0 at Hamburg after an 88th-minute Miro Muheim winner. Elsewhere, promoted Elversberg continued their impressive debut season in the top flight, winning 4-3 at home to Augsburg. Lukas Petkov, Lasse Guenther, Maximilian Rohr and Frederik Schmahl scored as Elversberg, from the smallest town to ever host a Bundesliga side, climbed to sixth in the table. Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the fifth straight Bundesliga match as his brace helped Werder Bremen come from two goals down to draw 2-2 at home to Paderborn. A first-half goal from Phillip Tietz was enough for Mainz to win 1-0 at Schalke and climb to fifth in the standings. AFP The post Diaz dazzles as Bayern Munich batter Leipzig 6-1 to go top appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: One in three adults in Pakistan lives with psychological disorder: study
items.description: KARACHI: Pakistan’s first nationally representative mental health survey has shown that nearly one in three adults is living with a diagnosable mental and behavioural disorder, highlighting a major public health challenge affecting millions of people across the country. The findings come from the largest and most comprehensive mental health study ever conducted in Pakistan, say researchers representing the Pakistan Psychiatric Society (PPS). The five-year research is published in the British Medical Journal. The survey was led by Professor Raza-ur-Rahman from Hamdard University, Karachi, in collaboration with Brighton and Sussex Medical School UK, University of South Florida, US, and psychiatric institutions across Pakistan. Experts term findings of first national mental health survey ‘most reliable’ Nearly 18,000 adults from all four provinces participated in the 2018-2022 study, providing the first nationally representative picture of mental health in the country. Key findings The study found that 32 per cent of adults were currently living with mental and behavioural disorders, while 38 per cent had experienced a disorder during their lifetime. One in five adults met criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). More than one in 10 adults had depression, whereas six per cent reported suicidal thoughts in the previous month. Researchers also identified significant social inequalities in mental health. Higher rates of mental disorders were found among older adults, individuals with lower levels of education and income, unemployed people, and those who were widowed, divorced or separated. Mental health problems were associated with substantial impairment in family life, social relationships and the ability to work. “This survey provides the evidence needed to develop effective mental health policies and services in Pakistan. It identifies who is most at risk, where support is most needed, and the scale of the unmet need for care,” said lead investigator Prof Raza-ur-Rahman, currently heading the department of psychiatry at HU. According to him, the researchers used international standard tools to carry out the survey and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics identified the areas for survey and provided the sample size. He hoped that it would contribute to reducing stigma and improving access to diagnosis and treatment for millions of people. “For the first time, policymakers, healthcare planners and researchers now have reliable national data that can be used to strengthen mental health services, allocate resources more effectively and develop evidence-based programmes across the country,” he added. The study represents a major milestone for mental health research in Pakistan and demonstrates the country’s growing capacity to undertake large-scale, internationally recognised public health research. Prof Anjum Memon, Chair in Epidemiology and Public Health Medicine at Brighton and Sussex Medical School (UK) and the senior co-author of the study, said: “This is a landmark moment for mental health research in Pakistan. For decades, policymakers have Memon, Chair in Epidemiology and Public Health Medicine at Brighton and Sussex Medical School (UK) and the senior co-author of the study, said: “This is a landmark moment for mental health research in Pakistan. For decades, policymakers have had to rely on fragmented local studies or international estimates. We now have robust national evidence showing, for the first time, the true scale of mental and behavioural disorders across the country.” These findings provide an invaluable evidence base for policymakers, clinicians and healthcare planners, not only in Pakistan but also in other low- and middle-income countries facing similar challenges, he added. Mental health, researchers say, is increasingly recognised as an essential component of national health and economic development and they recommend greater integration of mental health services into primary healthcare, increased investment in community-based support systems, enhanced training for frontline health workers and sustained national efforts to reduce the stigma surrounding mental illness. “Pakistan currently faces major challenges in the provision of mental healthcare, including limited specialist services and a shortage of trained mental health professionals. The survey findings will help inform future policy development, service planning, workforce training and community-based support programmes,” said President of PPS Prof Wajid Akhundzada. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Digging for Red Line damages gas pipeline, disrupts supply in Karachi
items.description: KARACHI: Gas supply to several areas of the metropolis was suspended during lunch hours on Saturday after a high-pressure pipeline was damaged during excavation work for the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line on University Road, adding to the miseries of residents in the affected areas. The disruption affected Gulshan-i-Iqbal, areas around Mazar-i-Quaid, parts of Garden, Saddar, Burns Road and several other localities. A spokesperson for the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) said that the high-pressure pipeline near the Gulshan-i-Iqbal telephone exchange on University Road was damaged at around 1pm during BRT construction activity. She said teams immediately reached the site and started repair work, which was completed by 5pm. “After completion of the work, gas supply was restored,” she said. Residents in the affected areas said the sudden suspension caused considerable inconvenience, particularly during cooking hours. Several households reported disruption in preparing afternoon meals, while commercial eateries and roadside hotels in Saddar and Garden saw a rush of customers as many people had no option but to dine out or take food home for their families. Domestic consumers complained that low pressure persisted even after the announced restoration time. Many families said they had to arrange food from nearby restaurants. “We had guests at home and the gas suddenly disappeared. We had to order biryani from a nearby hotel, which cost us extra besides causing embarrassment,” said Rozina Adnan, a resident of Saddar. Another resident from Garden said his wife could not cook and they had to bring food from a restaurant for the children. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Ouagadougou / Arrondissement 12 : L’école du mérite célébrée en modèle de citoyenneté
items.description: Les officiels lors de l'exécution de l'hymne national avant le début de la cérémonie relative à la journée de l'excellence scolaire à l'arrondissement 12 C'est une matinée qui aura marqué les esprits dans l'arrondissement 12 de Ouagadougou. Ce 14 octobre 2026, l'arrondissement 12 a vibré au rythme de la cinquième édition de la Journée de l'excellence scolaire, une célébration qui dépasse le simple rituel scolaire pour s'affirmer comme un véritable acte de patriotisme. Placée sous le thème « Célébrer l'excellence scolaire, reconnaître le mérite et promouvoir une culture de la réussite dans l'arrondissement 12 », la cérémonie a voulu rappeler une conviction essentielle : il n'y a pas de nation forte sans école forte, ni de développement durable sans culture du mérite. Les élèves ont répondu présent à la 5e journée de l'excellence scolaire à l'arrondissement 12 Dès les premières heures, le ton a été donné par l'exécution solennelle du Ditanyè, entonné avec ferveur et repris en chœur par des centaines d'élèves en acclamation. Un moment de communion républicaine qui a planté le décor d'une journée dédiée à l'effort et à l'exemplarité. Présidée par Zalissa Salembéré / Paré, présidente de la délégation spéciale de l'arrondissement 12, la cérémonie était placée sous le parrainage de Rasmané Konvolbo, PDG du groupe d'alimentation Bon Samaritain, et le co-parrainage de Souleymane Boly, représentant d'Endeavour Mining. Deux acteurs économiques qui ont fait le choix d'investir dans le capital le plus précieux : le capital humain. La présidente de la délégation spéciale, Zalissa SALEMBERE/ PARE a salué la performance scolaire au sein de son arrondissement et a exhorté les élèves à maintenir le cap Et le message est passé. En distinguant les meilleurs élèves mais aussi les enseignants les plus méritants, l'arrondissement 12 a voulu consacrer le travail bien fait comme valeur cardinale. Vélos pour faciliter la mobilité scolaire, kits complets et tableaux d'honneur ont été remis aux lauréats sous les ovations d'une foule conquise, comme autant d'invitations à persévérer. Au nom des récipiendaires, Mariam Haya a pris la parole avec une maturité qui a forcé l'admiration. Elle a pris l'engagement, au nom de tous les lauréats, de continuer à travailler avec ardeur pour honorer leurs écoles, leurs familles et tout l'arrondissement. Parrain de l'événement, Rasmané Konvolbo a salué une initiative qui fonde l'avenir sur le mérite, la responsabilité et le travail. Pour le PDG de Bon Samaritain, célébrer l'excellence, c'est préparer une société plus juste et plus forte. Il a félicité l'arrondissement 12 pour sa constance et réaffirmé sa disponibilité à accompagner durablement toute initiative qui place l'éducation au cœur du progrès collectif. Plusieurs lots dont des vélos ont été remis aux élèves méritants La présidente de la délégation spéciale n'a pas caché, elle non plus, sa fierté. Zalissa Salembéré / Paré a tenu à ancrer cette journée comme un levier de développement et non comme une simple fête. Chiffres à l'appui, elle a démontré la dynamique ascendante de la circonscription : sur 1 420 candidats présentés dont 720 filles, 1 095 admis au Certificat d'études primaires, soit un taux de succès de 98,24% contre 95,28% en 2025. Mieux, 31 écoles ont réalisé un sans-faute avec 100% de réussite. Une performance qui hisse l'arrondissement 12 au rang de deuxième meilleure performance scolaire de la commune de Ouagadougou. En s'adressant aux lauréats, elle les a invités à l'humilité et à la constance dans l'apprentissage, tout en ayant un mot d'encouragement pour ceux qui n'ont pas été distingués cette année : l'excellence est un chemin, pas une ligne d'arrivée. Elle a salué le rôle irremplaçable des enseignants et des parents d'élèves, véritables artisans de cette réussite, et témoigné sa gratitude au patron de la cérémonie, le président de la délégation spéciale de la commune, aux parrains, au comité d'organisation et à tous les acteurs mobilisés. La fête s'est achevée en beauté, entre animations culturelles et remise solennelle des prix, sous les applaudissements nourris du public. Plus qu'une cérémonie de récompense, l'arrondissement 12 vient de donner une leçon : quand l'école célèbre le mérite, c'est toute la nation qui se met debout. L’article Ouagadougou / Arrondissement 12 : L'école du mérite célébrée en modèle de citoyenneté est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Hunters kill kidnappers who came for ₦10m ransom in Kano
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State. This was contained in a statement by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer on Saturday. According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom “The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release. According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release. The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest. “During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said. The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident. The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area. Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura. Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect. He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group. The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family. The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property. Vanguard News The post Hunters kill kidnappers who came for ₦10m ransom in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Safe spaces for women
items.description: THE Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, was an important response to problems that directly affect women. It enabled the ombudsman to hear cases, many of which were resolved in women’s favour. A recent judgement has now eliminated an avenue that many women used to report harassment. The Federal Constitutional Court’s ruling , which narrows the interpretation of harassment, is a setback for women’s space in public life. Unfortunately, it appears to show that a major state institution is prepared to restrict rather than expand women’s safety at work. From birth to death, women and girls in Pakistan face limits on where they can go freely, where they may go only under certain conditions, and where they cannot go at all. Visitors to Pakistan often notice their limited visibility as one of the first features of public life. This absence should not be dismissed as cultural; it largely reflects structural factors. Restrictions on mobility — driven mainly by concerns about safety — help explain poor educational outcomes for girls, physical inactivity during adolescence, and their alarmingly low participation in the labour force as adults. The lack of safety outside the home is among the most frequently cited reasons for not sending girls to school, alongside poverty and families’ inability to afford schooling. The problem is intensified by the limited availability of girls’ schools in many parts of Pakistan. Undoubtedly, the shortage of schools and female teachers, together with poor learning quality, creates major barriers. Millions of girls live in districts where the nearest public school is more than an hour away and therefore out of practical reach. These supply-side failures prevent many girls from even imagining that they could enter a classroom. Perceived danger reinforces the barrier at home: some girls never enrol, while others drop out at puberty. At the very least, girls who are fortunate enough to live near a school should not be excluded because the journey is unsafe. Women’s limited ability to work outside the home is probably the most affected by structural factors. A Population Council and Unicef study, Adolescent Girls’ Voices on Enhancing Their Own Productivity, found that parents were reluctant to send girls to school because of fear of harassment on the way. This fear has been exacerbated by an incredible surge in social media-related harassment and cyberbullying, thanks to the proliferation of mobile phones and other digital devices. Requiring a chaperone or private transport immediately increases the costs of sending girls to school. Not surprisingly, an estimated 8.3 million girls aged 10 to 19 lack official status — they are neither in school, at work, nor married. This large cohort of girls depicts a decade of lost productivity, learning, and, above all, self-esteem. The state’s role is clear: protect the rights of all its citizens from harassment and unsafe spaces. It must remove these hurdles by providing structural solutions that enable girls to attend and complete school. Harassment laws that create safe routes and workplaces must be seen as educational policy requirements, not peripheral issues. Women’s limited ability to work outside the home is probably the most affected by structural factors. It is also the most costly in terms of losses to the economy and society. Female labour force participation rates have remained stagnant at around 22 per cent for the last 15 years. When women earn, they tend to spend more proactively, with direct payoffs for children’s education, health, and general welfare. But this will not happen if women feel unprotected at the workplace. Although women are generally accepted as schoolteachers and in some health professions, attacks on doctors and Lady Health Workers threaten even these spaces — many work mostly out of economic desperation. Employers are reluctant to give women jobs with longer, more secure contracts because of perceived hazards and domestic duties. At the other end of the spectrum, highly educated and affluent women participate in the labour force, cushioned by family support and private transport. The result is some improvement in women’s participation at the top end for highly educated, privileged women and, at the other end, for the truly desperate who must leave home to buy food and ensure their families’ survival, ie, domestic help, cleaners, and informal sector workers who do the most menial work. Women’s representation in Pakistan’s parliament is the only positive achievement in the SDGs’ gender indicators. Most elected women come from privileged families, but not all, as the pool expands. The trend began with the mandatory party quota for women. Otherwise, trends of an even more male-dominated parliament would have continued. The handful of women lawmakers have made headway in legislating, or at least highlighting, issues important to women and human rights. Comparable action is required in laws and public policy to expand women’s participation in every public sphere, especially formal employment. Increasing the number of women in decision-making and other critical positions — particularly in the police and judiciary — would make a tangible difference. A 30pc recruitment quota in the formal sector is essential. Greater representation in formal paid work will generate positive spillover effects in other sectors. It is especially imperative to address the extremely high unemployment rate (24pc) among young women who have completed more than a secondary education. Despite completing higher levels of education, this group is denied opportunities for secure employment. A quota system and positive supportive legislation will directly and positively affect the current generation whom we repeatedly say we care about the most. Women and girls must have safe passage and be guarded with assurances that harassment is a punishable offence. Recent measures to improve women’s mobility are encouraging, such as pink buses and scooter loans, but they remain too few and too far apart. Above all, there is a need to change mindsets; a public campaign against harassment of women and girls in public spaces must become a priority. Society must review its standards and morals and move forward, not backwards, in legislation, run bold campaigns, and do whatever it takes to correct this pernicious course of restricting, rather than expanding, the power of women and girls. The writer is country adviser to the Population Council. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Arguments sought on defamation suit against PTI founder
items.description: LAHORE: A sessions court on Saturday sought arguments from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s counsel on a miscellaneous application by a lawyer for PTI founding chairman Imran Khan seeking permission to meet his client in jail regarding a Rs10 billion defamation suit filed by the former against the latter. Earlier, Khan’s counsel, Muhammad Hussain Chotia, argued for permission to meet his client at Adiala Jail, Rawalpindi, saying he needed instructions from him regarding the case and his signatures on documents. He told the court that the jail authorities were not allowing the meeting. He asked the court to direct the jail superintendent to permit him to meet Khan. Additional District & Sessions Judge Yalmaz Ghani adjourned the hearing till Oct 31 and sought arguments from the prime minister’s lawyer. In his suit filed in 2017, Prime Minister Shehbaz said Imran Khan levelled baseless allegations against him in connection with the Panama Papers controversy. He sought a decree for recovery of Rs10bn as compensation from the defendant for publication of defamatory content. Several key government figures, including Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Ahmad Khan have already recorded their statements in support of the plaintiff, the prime minister. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Closing the Afghan file
items.description: THE civil-military relationship in Pakistan has never been ideal. Despite recent conciliatory efforts and the policy of accommodation adopted by the coalition government, concerns within security-focused circles persist about the handling of several government affairs. For now, though, there is little chance of an escalation in civil-military tensions involving the federal and provincial governments; the last hitch was the PTI government, which was ousted through governor’s rule and emergency . The major allegation against the PTI government has been that it was hesitant to take a clear position against the terrorists, enabling them to expand their influence in parts of the province, especially in the southern districts. The establishment is sensitive about the narrative, and considers it subversion and part of hybrid warfare; it looks upon any political or ideological support for it as support to the enemy. Terminology describing Taliban-aligned terrorists as ‘Fitna al-Khwarij’ and Baloch insurgents as ‘Fitna al-Hindustan’ reflects the same approach. Everyone is expected to follow this approach; the PTI government’s disagreement on several security-related policies is, therefore, interpreted as an act of subversion. Meanwhile, it is clear how much civilian governments actually contribute to security-related affairs. The security domain has often caused friction between the establishment and civilian governments; over the decades, the political leadership has learned not to voice disagreement on security-related affairs. ‘Memogate’ was the last such lesson for the PPP; and ‘ Dawn leaks’ for Mian Nawaz Sharif; the removal of Imran Khan’s PTI from its provincial seat of power in KP appears to have followed the same pattern. The story is not simply about subversion or disagreement over security policy. There are other relevant aspects that some commentators have pointed out: among them is the fiscal issue which also triggered the call for new provinces and the reversal of the 18th Amendment. Yet another dimension is linked to closing the Afghan file. Bhutto’s policy was just the lever. It was Zia who turned it into an ideology. The Afghan policy has shaped Pakistan’s politics for half a century; but now there is a general acceptance, even within security circles, that it has not worked. It is evident that the state is distancing itself from past approaches. In this regard, some intellectuals and commentators have painted militancy as a cultural expression of Pakhtuns, which the local dynamics of the larger Pakhtun society has aggravated. There is no need to deconstruct such a perception, which would be stigmatisation. In effect, applying a sociocultural lens to the issue takes away focus from the main architects of the security and Afghan policy. The previous Afghan policy worked well but had lost its utility in geopolitical contexts. This was the policy crafted by the military dictator Gen Ziaul Haq and his team, and it was more or less functional until the Taliban captured power in Afghanistan in August 2021. Though the Zia file saw a few changes and amendments, the overall framework for dealing with these affairs did not change much. The Zia file had a few critical components that even allies including Washington, Beijing, Riyadh, and Ankara had concerns about — particularly the reliance on non-state actors. Mian Nawaz Sharif had drawn attention to it but faced the consequences. Many analysts believe that this flawed policy was responsible for spawning the TTP and generating terrorism in KP but official narratives do not link the state of affairs to the policy choices made earlier. Establishment circles appear to want a new Afghan policy that best suits their geopolitical and internal security objectives. A complete detachment from the Taliban is part of the new approach, and the Sohail Afridi government was reluctant to adopt it because it would mean a large-scale military operation, displacement, and increased security-related resource allocation — which would also have political consequences. After the removal of his government, the hurdles preventing a new policy have been eliminated; the new set-up now has to deliver, as was expected of the Afridi government. There will be no opportunity any longer to shift the onus of blame onto a political government, despite official narratives distancing the security state from political change in KP. However, the dimensions of the new Afghan policy remain unclear. For instance, how will the state proceed if the Afghan Taliban agree to detach themselves from the terrorist networks operating against Pakistan from Afghan soil? Still, another argument being promoted is that Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, not Gen Ziaul Haq, was the real architect of Pakistan’s Afghan policy. There is some truth to that. After Sardar Daud’s 1973 coup in Kabul and his revival of the Pakhtunistan issue, the Bhutto government began hosting and training Afghan Islamists, among them men who would later become the commanders of the anti-Soviet jihad. The FC and a small circle of officials ran this as a pressure tool against Kabul. Notably, the province’s first governor after 1973, appointed in 1975, following the ban on the National Awami Party, reflected the same anxieties about Pakhtun nationalism and Afghanistan. But Bhutto’s policy was just the lever. It was Zia who turned it into an ideology. After the Soviet invasion of 1979, the Afghan question became the organising principle of the state: the jihad, the refugee economy, the madressah network, the doctrine of strategic depth, and an intelligence apparatus that grew more powerful than the elected institutions meant to oversee it. That legacy matters, and it is Zia’s. Now it is up to the supporters of the PPP how they take the argument, and whether they are ready to carry the entire burden of history on their shoulders; they also face criticism that Benazir Bhutto continued Bhutto’s legacy and allowed Gen Naseerullah Babar to nurture the Taliban in 1994-96, the same general who had crafted the Afghan files for her father. The Taliban generations have caused huge losses to the PPP, including the assassination of Benazir Bhutto herself. The writer is a security analyst. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Francia prende fuego al macronismo
items.description: Francia salió a la calle el 17 de octubre de 2026 y, entre manifestaciones, incendios y pillajes, certificó la muerte del macronismo . Lo hizo con violencia, como suele hacerlo. Rabia, cólera y también miedo hacia el futuro. Y lo que constató mientras destrozaba comercios e incendiaba ayuntamientos y comisarías fue la defunción de una idea política que quería instaurar una centralidad ideológica radical y contener el auge de los extremos. En lugar de eso, fueron nueve años en los que se vaciaron los servicios públicos, se multiplicó la deuda (pasó del 98% del PIB al 119% actual) y los polos ideológicos en el Parlamento engulleron el debate público hasta ser hoy las dos fuerzas políticas —la izquierdista La Francia Insumisa (LFI) y el ultraderechista Reagrupamiento Nacional (RN)— con más posibilidades de llegar a la segunda vuelta en las elecciones de la próxima primavera. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un frente de izquierdas y otro de derechas se disputarán a cara de perro el control del Senado
items.description: El Senado no será un campo de batalla secundario sino central en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. Mientras en el Congreso, las distintas opciones políticas concurrirán por separado —muchas fuerzas a la izquierda del PSOE se han agrupado en el llamado Frente Amplio, del que se han excluido Podemos y los nacionalistas catalanes, vascos o gallegos—, en el Senado se están configurando dos bloques mayoritarios, una de derechas y otro de izquierdas, enfrentados a cara de perro. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Aitor Esteban: “Nadie ha demostrado más con hechos que no queremos a Vox”
items.description: Desde hace meses, Aitor Esteban (Bilbao, 64 años) venía advirtiendo de que al Gobierno de coalición se le acababa el combustible. Hace dos semanas, 48 horas antes de que el Congreso tumbase los decretos de vivienda , el presidente del PNV viajó a Madrid y ya barruntaba en privado que Pedro Sánchez podría estar sopesando la convocatoria electoral , aun en el caso de que ganase las votaciones. “Para él era como cambiar de ventana después de que todo estuviese centrado en Ceuta”, comentaba Esteban el pasado viernes en Sabin Etxea, la sede central del PNV en Bilbao. “La legislatura tenía que tener un propósito, no gobernar por gobernar, solo resistir. Ya no tenía sentido”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los dos grandes creen que la campaña se va colocando donde querían
items.description: Al ver las imágenes de Pedro Sánchez bailando eufórico al final del gran mitin de consagración de su candidatura en Fuenlabrada, la pregunta surge natural: ¿tan convencido está el líder del PSOE de que puede repetir el milagro de 2023 y seguir en La Moncloa? Según distintas personas de su entorno consultadas, no se trata de una pose, aunque todo candidato está obligado a trasladar entusiasmo si quiere que le voten. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Feijóo, contra los fantasmas de 2023
items.description: La tarde de las elecciones generales del 3 de marzo de 1996 , Pedro Arriola entró en el despacho de José María Aznar en la calle Génova anunciando el fracaso. Fuera se escuchaban a todo volumen los gritos de los simpatizantes del PP coreando “¡Pujol, enano, habla castellano!”, así que Miguel Ángel Rodríguez ordenó al técnico de sonido del PP que subiera al máximo los decibelios de la música para mitigar los cánticos. Con el sonido del bullicio entrando por las ventanas del despacho de Aznar, Arriola tragó saliva y soltó: “Hemos perdido las elecciones”. El entonces líder del PP se revolvió en su asiento y se indignó ante su asesor de cabecera: “¿Pero cómo puede ser que hayamos perdido, si el viernes sacábamos ocho puntos de distancia al PSOE?“. Arriola estaba equivocado y Aznar ganó las elecciones esa noche pero, a diferencia de la amplia victoria que pronosticaban las encuestas, lo hizo con una estrechísima distancia del PSOE, de tan solo 290.000 votos y poco más de un punto porcentual con Felipe González. Así que se vio forzado a gobernar con el apoyo del mismo Pujol contra el que coreaban sus militantes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ocho décadas después, un anciano de 105 años debe responder por los crímenes del nazismo
items.description: J. S. es uno de los vecinos más conocidos de un pequeño municipio del oeste de Alemania. Tiene 105 años, los medios locales le dedican artículos por su aniversario desde que es un venerable centenario y el alcalde lo recibe con honores. Lo que muchos de sus conciudadanos no saben es que también fue guardia en el mayor campo de prisioneros de guerra en Alemania durante la II Guerra Mundial , el Stalag 326. Al menos 15.000 presos, sobre todo combatientes soviéticos, murieron allí en condiciones inhumanas, aunque se cree que la cifra real puede ascender a 70.000. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El colosal reto de evaluar a los universitarios en la era de la IA: ¿prohibirla o usarla como aliada?
items.description: Mucho ha llovido en la prestigiosa Universidad de Brown (Estados Unidos) desde que su catedrático Roberto Serrano denunciase en este diario en junio un fraude masivo con inteligencia artificial (IA) en uno de sus exámenes, sin que el decanato reaccionase. La noticia fue replicada por los principales medios ―hasta la revista Nature le pidió un artículo―, Serrano ha recibido “cientos” de cartas de apoyo y la persona que estaba al frente del Comité del Código Académico ha sido cesada. Pero lo que más conmueve al eminente economista español es que cree que sus alumnos han aprendido la lección. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las vacaciones familiares en Bélgica que terminaron con el arresto de un sicario huido de la justicia
items.description: Vacaciones. Una semana en Bélgica . Ruta por ciudades como Bruselas y Brujas. También por los canales de Gante, última parada antes de regresar a Málaga. Allí pasaba la última noche del viaje un inspector de la Policía Nacional junto a su familia. Decidieron salir a cenar y, después, recorrer las callejuelas del casco histórico. Durante el paseo, móvil en mano, él quedó retrasado unos metros. Seguir leyendo Un fugitivo en una tienda de muebles Por extraño que parezca, no es la primera vez que este mismo inspector se topa con un fugitivo de la justicia por casualidad. Ocurrió también hace unos años, esta vez en casa, cuando iba de compras con su familia a IKEA. Aquella vez estaba inmerso en una investigación en la que junto a sus compañeros fotografiaron un rostro desconocido para ellos. Ya en comisaría intentaron ponerle nombre y un agente que pasaba por allí pensó que se trataba de un fugitivo de Estonia buscado por un homicidio y que llevaba años huido de la justicia. Compararon fotos y no, resultó que no era aquel hombre. Tres días después, y sin haber oído nada sobre él anteriormente, justo se cruzó con ese delincuente estonio cuando se encontraba en el establecimiento de muebles. Avisó a su grupo y al 091. Minutos más tarde, sus compañeros, junto a las patrullas enviadas por la sala, consiguieron arrestarle en el aparcamiento.

items.title: Hermana, no es la ideología
items.description: Hace un tiempo, el psiquiatra mallorquín Miquel Roca y yo anduvimos fantaseando con hacer retratos de orden psicológico a figuras políticas. Todo fluía, con humor incluso, con personajes del pasado, pero llegábamos al presente y, ay, se corría el peligro de patologizar cualquier comportamiento. Escudriñar la mente, el corazón o el intestino (allá donde quiera que se refugie la ética) puede llevarte de la comprensión al perdón, o de la admiración al desprecio. En el crudo ambiente político que vivimos, los hay que hacen pinitos psicologistas con brocha gorda: abundan, por ejemplo, aquellos que acusan al presidente Sánchez de defender los principios de igualdad y fraternidad sobre los que se construyó la Europa nacida de la Segunda Guerra Mundial movido únicamente por la espuria intención de revitalizar su imagen ante la izquierda desmovilizada. Es decir, que más que luchar por el bien común, el ladino presidente estaría batallando por seguir gozando del célebre Falcon. Si así fuera, si aceptamos que Sánchez defiende lo que es justo movido por una ambición desmedida, no me encuentro en condiciones de juzgarlo, porque, hoy, es más urgente la misión política que la sinceridad del jugador. ¿Cómo llegamos a su mente, corazón o intestino? ¿con el célebre polígrafo? Además ¿de qué serviría? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Gabriel Rufián es un genio
items.description: Lo mínimo que puede decirse de Gabriel Rufián es que es un genio. Desde hace meses, según los estudios de opinión, el portavoz de Esquerra Republicana aparece como el político más valorado y al que se deseaba como aglutinador del frente de guerra de guerrillas que ha demostrado ser la infantil izquierda a la izquierda. Lo ha conseguido a pesar de una doble paradoja. La primera tiene que ver con su vinculación al proyecto que lo creó y catapultó: no es fácil descifrar como un independentista ha engatusado a un votante concienciado de Malasaña, haciéndole olvidar que su principal objetivo, en teoría, era conseguir la secesión de una de las regiones más ricas de España, con lo que quebraría la solidaridad interterritorial. A la vez, segunda paradoja, su dominio de las redes sociales de segunda generación ha actuado como un somnífero viral que ha logrado borrar de la memoria un episodio clave de su actividad parlamentaria. Él ―ese hombre de la calle que se atreve a decir las verdades en comisiones de investigación y la tribuna del Congreso― fue el dirigente que más seriamente puso en riesgo la iniciativa social más determinante de los gobiernos de Pedro Sánchez: la reforma laboral. En aquella ocasión su ángel de la guarda fue un diputado popular que se confundió al votar. Pero si el no defendido entonces por Rufián hubiese tumbado aquella reforma consensuada por el Ministerio de Trabajo con los agentes sociales, ¿habría logrado culminar la exitosa transformación de su personaje? Lo dudo. Pero sería un error infravalorarlo. Hace cuatro días ha conseguido llegar a un pacto con Podemos, a pesar de que el partido de Pablo Iglesias fue claro al valorar el principal proyecto de Esquerra Republicana de esta legislatura en Cataluña. “Nace muerta”, sentenció Ione Belarra, sobre la reforma del modelo de financiación. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Gran Reemplazo europeo
items.description: ¿Recuerdan cuando la UE reconvenía a estados como Hungría o Polonia cuando sus gobiernos recortaban derechos, cuando debatíamos cómo controlar sus desmanes iliberales? Esta semana, en el Consejo Europeo celebrado en Bruselas, la primera ministra danesa, la socialdemócrata Mette Frederiksen, con el respaldo entusiasta de la posfascista Giorgia Meloni, invirtió de forma oficial esa lógica al pedir que se examinara a España no por recortar derechos, sino por reconocérselos a medio millón de personas mediante un proceso de regularización. Esa inversión dice mucho sobre el estado de la Unión, pues Europa servía precisamente para proteger los derechos individuales frente a las mayorías y acervos nacionales, mientras hoy, de forma falaz, cuando nadie puede afirmar que la regularización viole norma alguna, se apuesta abiertamente por una política migratoria , mayoritaria en Europa, donde los derechos, pensados para no someterse a votación, pueden revisarse y cercenarse cuando así lo quieren nuestros gobiernos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El todopoderoso alcalde que llevó al PP a una crisis anunciada en Algeciras
items.description: Una señora mayor con el brazo escayolado reconoce al todavía alcalde de Algeciras (Cádiz) y exsenador del PP, José Ignacio Landaluce, en una plaza del centro de la ciudad gaditana este viernes. Se acerca a él con pasitos cortos: “He visto todo lo que está saliendo en la tele y quiero que sepas que no me creo nada”, le dice con una sonrisa. Landaluce le devuelve el gesto, le da las gracias y le lanza un beso. La mujer alude a las denuncias presentadas por dos afiliadas del PP por presuntas agresiones sexuales contra el dirigente. Unas horas después de ese encuentro, el Juzgado de Violencia sobre la Mujer de Algeciras cita a Landaluce para declarar como imputado el próximo 23 de octubre por una de ellas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El despido de la portavoz de Trump desliza a la Casa Blanca hacia el caos a dos semanas de las ‘midterms’
items.description: La segunda presidencia de Donald Trump, se dijo, no iba a ser como la primera. Él llegaba tras una travesía en el desierto, pero con las lecciones aprendidas; rodeado de un ejército de fieles, y no, como en 2017, de un equipo de colaboradores dispuestos a llevarle la contraria de vez en cuando. Tampoco sería, como sí fue aquella, un incesante espectáculo de filtraciones, puñaladas entre bambalinas y despidos impulsivos a golpe de tuit. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ucrania, en punto muerto: asediada por Putin y abandonada por Trump
items.description: Amanece con lluvia en Kramatorsk, bastión ucranio bajo amenaza rusa en el frente oriental. Lo que supone un problema para que los drones vuelen se convierte en una oportunidad para que la infantería del Kremlin trate de ganar terreno. Se trata, en todo caso, de pequeñas escaramuzas. Así lo observa EL PAÍS desde un puesto de mando militar en Kramatorsk a través de imágenes captadas por los drones el jueves pasado. La línea del frente no sufre apenas cambios y la guerra está atrapada en una compleja maraña camino del quinto aniversario de la gran invasión rusa. Kiev, además, cierra una semana en la que se ha llevado serios reveses. Por un lado, en casa, los ataques sobre una veintena de sus regiones y, por otro, en la arena internacional, el revolcón que supone el indisimulado alineamiento de Estados Unidos con Rusia . Seguir leyendo

items.title: La batalla contra el ‘pinkwashing’ en las campañas del cáncer de mama: “Si has ganado un millón de euros, no me des los centimillos”
items.description: En octubre, todo es rosa. Los edificios, los enormes carteles de publicidad, los spots de televisión, las publicaciones en Instagram y hasta el lazo perfectamente ubicado en la americana de altas autoridades europeas, como el de la presidenta de la Comisión, Ursula von der Leyen . Casi ni hace falta mencionarlo, pero ese color, en esta época del año, solo puede significar una cosa: la lucha contra el cáncer de mama. Está instalado en el inconsciente colectivo. Se asume que todas las empresas que se suman a esta iniciativa apoyan, de alguna manera, a las mujeres que son diagnosticadas con la enfermedad , 37.000 cada año en el caso de España. Pero esto no siempre es así. Diferentes organizaciones llevan años cuestionando a las marcas que impulsan campañas para incentivar la compra de productos de edición especial, pero que solo donan porcentajes mínimos a las asociaciones o que lanzan un mensaje esperanzador, centrado en la prevención, sin hablar de las 18 mujeres que mueren al día por cáncer de mama en España o sin incluir los reclamos de las pacientes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La alta velocidad entre Barcelona y Madrid pierde frecuencias, fiabilidad y rapidez
items.description: La estación de Sants en Barcelona es un enjambre de personas. Es miércoles. En la vía número tres, hay una cola enorme para ir a Girona. En la cuatro, sin embargo, apenas hay gente esperando para acceder al AVE que conecta Barcelona con Madrid. El tren, que debía salir a las 15.00, sigue inmóvil. No partirá hasta, al menos, las 15.25. Para esa hora hay otro convoy programado, pero en la estación ya advierten de que también partirá con retraso. Dentro del tren, Marta se lo toma con filosofía. “Por suerte, no tengo prisa. No es la primera vez que me pasa. Cuando vi en las noticias el incendio ya me imaginé que esto iba a ir mal”, se resigna. No lo ve igual Jesús, que durante todo el viaje protesta por teléfono: “Un viaje que hacíamos en dos horas y media ahora lo hacemos en cuatro. Yo tenía una audiencia esta mañana en Barcelona y ya me vine anoche. Para otra ocasión, iré en avión”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Viaje al Studio Ghibli: el presente lento y el futuro misterioso de la animación eterna
items.description: Uno de los grandes temas de las películas del dibujante japonés Hayao Miyazaki es cómo entran en contacto mundos que pertenecen a dimensiones muy diferentes. En Mi vecino Totoro o El viaje de Chihiro , sus personajes cruzan el umbral desde la realidad hasta un universo misterioso, a veces temible, a veces reconfortante. El genial cineasta japonés no explica cómo se produce esa transición. Simplemente, ocurre. Espectadores de todo el mundo se preguntan si alguna vez tendrán la oportunidad de volver a realizar ese viaje con una nueva película de Studio Ghibli , la productora de animación japonesa que recibirá el próximo viernes en Oviedo el premio Princesa de Asturias de Comunicación y Humanidades sin que ese misterio se haya resuelto. Como tituló recientemente la revista Bloomberg Businessweek , “el gran secreto de Ghibli es qué viene ahora”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Pobreza, humor y una historia de amor con Pepita: la vida de Chiquito de la Calzada hecha serie
items.description: Septiembre. Playa, humedad, muchísimo calor. En un requiebro del paseo marítimo de Torremolinos (Málaga) hay una multitud que se acerca a una pareja que, a pesar de todo, camina, tranquila, del brazo. Tras alcanzarlos, les piden autógrafos, les dan las gracias, los celebran. Hasta que una voz grita: “¡Cortamos! La tenemos”. Las cámaras dejan de grabar, los extras se retiran y el perfil de los dos protagonistas emerge bajo un paraguas que les protege del sol. Es imposible confundirlos. Camino del set de rodaje van Chiquito de la Calzada y su inseparable Pepita, su mujer, su compañera, su amor de toda la vida. Lo hacen en la piel de Alfonso Sánchez e Inma Cuevas , actor y actriz principal de Chiquito el Grande , serie que rodaron durante ocho semanas de este verano entre Málaga y Sevilla. Se estrenará a lo largo de 2027 en RTVE. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Álex Corretja: “Una de las cosas más importantes del tenis y de la vida es saber borrar lo que acaba de suceder”
items.description: París, 10 de junio de 2001. Un tenista entra furioso en el vestuario en mitad de la final que está jugando en Roland Garros . Ha enviado un revés ganador fuera por un “puto centímetro” que hubiera roto el servicio de su rival y, de ganar su saque, ponerse dos sets arriba en el partido. Pero el set ha volado y ahora la final está en lo mejor: uno a uno. El tenista es Álex Corretja , que perdió la final del año anterior ante Carlos Moyá . Ha llegado de nuevo, esta vez contra el brasileño Guga Kuerten. La preparación ha sido absoluta. En lugar de hacer la pretemporada en diciembre, la hizo en enero. Se fue a Sierra Nevada para correr en altura y aumentar glóbulos rojos; se llevó un sparring, un colega para correr con él de liebre, preparador físico, entrenador, médicos, nutricionista. Todo enfocado a Roland Garros. Y ahora, con empate en el marcador, se mira al espejo y dice: “No vas a conseguir ganar nunca este puto torneo”. Sale a la pista y Kuerten le mete 6-2 / 6-0 en los dos siguientes sets. Seguir leyendo Estilismo: Ángela Esteban-Librero Maquillaje: David López (Another Artists Agency) Producción: Cristina Serrano Asistente de fotografía: Miguel Sancho Asistente de estilismo: Lidia Lara Asistente de producción: Marina Marco

items.title: Peter Thiel, el tecnoligarca que cree en el anticristo
items.description: Cuando Hulk Hogan demandó al medio sensacionalista Gawker en 2016 por la publicación sin su consentimiento de un vídeo de contenido sexual, nadie daba un duro por él. Pero Hogan ganó el juicio y consiguió una indemnización de 140 millones de dólares que acabó con la publicación online . Peter Thiel , uno de los personajes más siniestros de Silicon Valley, decantó la batalla judicial: financió en secreto a los abogados de Hogan. Quería vengarse de Gawker porque lo había ridiculizado durante años y desvelado su homosexualidad. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bastaría con querer hacerlo
items.description: Desde luego no ha sido la primera vez que sucede algo así, ni, por desgracia, era inesperado, pero el rechazo de los decretos de vivienda ha vuelto a dejarme anonadada. Se ve que las fuerzas políticas de nuestro país son incapaces de colaborar en causas esenciales, tan esenciales, en fin, que van mucho más allá de los valores partidistas y son transversales, afectando a toda la sociedad, sea cual sea su ideología. No digo que los decretos fueran perfectos ni suficientes. Todo es susceptible de mejora. Pero usar la catástrofe habitacional para arreciar en el pimpampum electoralista y politiquero me parece deprimente (además de que deben de estar sordos y miopes, dada la indignación que arde en las calles). Seguir leyendo

items.title: María Neira, candidata española a dirigir la OMS: “Los nuevos desafíos exigen más ciencia y mejor comunicación”
items.description: Cada vez que alguien abre un grifo de agua, la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS) está detrás de ese gesto: establece las normas que garantizan su calidad. “También está detrás de la definición de qué tiene que llevar una crema para protegerte de los rayos ultravioletas”, asegura María Neira (La Felguera, Asturias, 64 años), la española que aspira a dirigir la OMS, para explicar el impacto en la vida cotidiana de una institución que pasa por horas bajas después de la retirada de la financiación de Estados Unidos y el desplome de su autoridad. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mikey Madison, la jinete tímida que ganó un Oscar y que ha decidido regresar a lo grande
items.description: Mikey Madison llegó, ganó y desapareció. Hace solo un par de temporadas, la actriz angelina, de 27 años, era el perejil de todas las salsas hollywoodienses. Tras una larga carrera de premios donde Demi Moore parecía imponerse en cada entrega, cuando llegaron los Oscar dio la sorpresa. Madison, prácticamente una completa desconocida, se alzó con la estatuilla a mejor actriz por su papel en Anora , donde interpretaba a una prostituta en un crudo retrato muy alejado de Pretty Woman y otros cuentos. Pero a su omnipresencia durante esa temporada de premios se impuso su discreción, y tras el Oscar desapareció. Ahora ha llegado el momento de su regreso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: State of denial
items.description: AS reports continue to do the rounds of possible Russian mediation to resolve the differences between Pakistan and Taliban-ruled Afghanistan, the Foreign Office has underscored that successful dialogue requires commitment from Kabul to end cross-border terrorism. This demand is neither new nor unreasonable; it highlights the point that talks and support for anti-Pakistan terrorist groups cannot go hand in hand. On Friday, the FO said that while it was not aware of any formal Russian mediation initiative, Pakistan was open to engagement that produced tangible results. Representatives of Pakistan and the Taliban regime were both in Russia earlier this month as part of the Moscow Format regional consultations. A joint communique could not be issued at the conclave due to frosty Islamabad-Kabul ties, specifically because the Taliban objected to including any references to terrorism in Afghanistan. Russia had offered its good offices to resolve the impasse, if both sides required its help. The official Taliban position amounts to a state of denial: it is hardly a secret that some of the world’s most dangerous terrorist groups find shelter in Afghanistan. Therefore, the Kabul regime’s denials hold no water. Many other third parties — Qatar, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, and China — have tried to mediate between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with varying degrees of success. Russia is the only state that recognises t he Taliban regime. Perhaps Moscow can be engaged by Pakistan and Afghanistan to try and give the peace process another chance. Pakistan and Afghanistan share borders and linguistic and cultural links. Good relations are essential, even though bilateral relations have remained largely strained over the past several decades. However, the biggest obstacle to long-term peace is the Taliban’s sheltering of terrorist groups. Pakistan desires peace, but for talks to succeed, Kabul must offer visible CBMs, such as an end to cross-border terrorism. As the FO has said, a “verifiable mechanism” that ensures an end to anti-Pakistan terrorism emanating from Afghanistan can lead the way to peace. Kabul’s claims that it is not hosting violent groups are of little value. Action against such groups is required, not hollow refutations. Moreover, regional states must realise that today it is Pakistan that is battling terrorist groups in Afghanistan. Tomorrow, similar violent actors based in that country can destabilise other regional states. Russia itself has been targeted by IS-K terrorism. The group finds a home in Afghanistan, even though it is at daggers drawn with the Taliban. If the Taliban regime commits to preventing groups based on its soil from attacking neighbouring states, the process of normalisation and regional integration of Afghanistan can begin. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi drones as Egypt weighs defensive support
items.description: A spokesman for the Saudi coalition said on October 17 that it had "intercepted and destroyed four drones over the past few hours in the regions of Riyadh, the Eastern Province, and the South"

items.description: Defense minister confirms fatalities as strong winds spread flames beyond base perimeter in Alberta, prompting large-scale emergency response

items.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has arrived in Bahrain, where on Sunday he will take part in the ninth round of the strategic dialogue between Russia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), a Sputnik correspondent has reported.

VK data center in Leningrad Region targeted by drone attack

items.title: Tanger : le FITUT revient pour sa 19è édition
items.description: La 19e édition du Festival international du théâtre universitaire de Tanger (FITUT) se tiendra du 26 au 30 octobre. Ce rendez-vous culturel et artistique vise à promouvoir la création théâtrale universitaire, à favoriser les échanges artistiques et culturels entre étudiants et professionnels et à valoriser le théâtre en tant qu’espace d’expression, de créativité et de dialogue entre les cultures, indique un communiqué des organisateurs. Cette manifestation ambitionne également de contribuer au rayonnement culturel et artistique de la ville de Tanger, en mettant en valeur les initiatives théâtrales universitaires et en favorisant l’ouverture sur différentes expériences artistiques et culturelles. Le jury de cette édition est composé de figures du théâtre et du paysage artistique marocain, notamment l’écrivain et metteur en scène El Meskini Sghir, les actrices Naïma Elias et Hajar Alsharki, ainsi que l’acteur Abderrahim El Meniari. Le programme prévoit une série de représentations au Palais des Arts et de la Culture et dans d’autres espaces de la ville, avec la participation d’établissements et d’institutions artistiques du Maroc, d’Espagne, de Pologne, d’Oman, des Pays-Bas, d’Arabie saoudite, du Portugal, d’Arménie et d’Italie. En parallèle des spectacles, des ateliers théâtraux et des séances d’échange et de débat à l’issue des représentations sont prévus, afin de favoriser les interactions entre les équipes artistiques et le public. À travers cette programmation, le FITUT entend consolider la place du théâtre universitaire comme espace de rencontre, de création et de dialogue interculturel, tout en contribuant au rayonnement culturel et artistique de Tanger. items.title: Balochistan CM Bugti urges Fazl to keep national security above politics
items.description: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti has said that law and order and national security in Balochistan should be treated as issues beyond political differences. He stressed that comparisons between the governments of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, particularly regarding terrorism and national security, must be based on ground realities and practical measures. The chief minister said he holds JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in high regard and that their personal relationship is based on mutual respect. In a statement posted on social media platform X, CM Bugti said the Maulana and his party had also been targeted in terrorist attacks. He expressed the hope that the JUI-F chief would take into account the state’s efforts to combat terrorism and the sacrifices made by security forces when commenting on this sensitive national issue. CM Bugti said the performance of the two provincial governments should be assessed on the basis of their counterterrorism measures, the conduct of their political leadership, and their commitment to eliminating terrorism. He said that despite political differences between the government and opposition in Balochistan, both sides had maintained a common position against terrorism, demonstrating a commitment to placing national interests above partisan considerations. The chief minister said his government regularly took the opposition into confidence on counterterrorism strategies, key decisions, and related matters in the Balochistan Assembly. He added that the provincial government was committed to taking all parliamentary parties along. He cited acknowledgements by Opposition Leader Mir Younis Aziz Zehri and a recent speech by Balochistan National Party (Mengal) parliamentary leader Mir Jahanzeb Mengal as evidence of the province’s political leadership recognising its responsibility in the fight against terrorism. CM Bugti said the JUI-F, the National Party, the BNP-Mengal, and other parliamentary parties shared a common stance against terrorism. He stressed that the fight against terrorism was not merely a matter of political statements or claims but a shared res­p­­o­­nsibility of the state and the entire nation. Pakistan, he said, was continuing its eff­­­orts to eliminate terrorism, while off­i­cers and personnel of the Pakistan Ar­­­­my and other security institutions were making extraordinary sacrifices in the struggle. Describing Maulana Fazlur Rehman as a senior politician whose party had also suffered human and political losses due to terrorism, CM Bugti said comparisons between the governments of KP and Balochistan must consider their practical counterterrorism measures, coordination among political leaders, and cooperation with state institutions. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Egypt ‘ready to defend’ Saudi Arabia against Houthis
items.description: • President Sisi says Cairo will take ‘any measure’ to protect kingdom if asked • Iran backs ‘political process’, offers to mediate • Saudi, Houthi forces trade fire CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi pledged on Saturday that Egypt was ready to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi forces if requested, as fighting intensified across the region and Cairo moved towards possible parliamentary authorisation for support. Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy, Sisi said Egypt was “not looking for a role to play” in regional conflicts but that it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was “harmed or its security and stability threatened”. “Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you,” Sisi said. He said any deployment would require parliamentary approval and expressed hope lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to authorise support “if it is requested of us”. “I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone,” Sisi said. “We are speaking only about defence.” Egyptian state media later reported that parliament would hold an emergency session on Sunday at Sisi’s request to consider possible support for Saudi defences. Egypt joined the Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen in 2015, though its role has largely focused on securing Red Sea shipping routes rather than frontline combat. The renewed conflict also threatens Egypt’s economic interests, particularly Suez Canal revenues. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last month that the Suez Canal had lost about $11 billion in revenue since the Houthis began attacking commercial vessels in 2023. During a visit to Egypt last month, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea. Egypt has not joined the Makkah agreement, a mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan in August, and has said it is studying the agreement. Sisi also said on Saturday that his presidential term would end in 2030 and proposed a 30-month training programme at the Egyptian Military Academy to prepare potential future leaders. He said a committee would develop selection criteria and legislation for the programme, which would target PhD holders from reputable Egyptian and foreign universities. Iran, meanwhile, backed a political solution to the Saudi-Houthi conflict and renewed its offer to mediate. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi repeated Iran’s offer to mediate between the two sides. Araghchi said on Saturday at the Organ­isation of Islamic Coope­ration in Baghdad that Tehran supported an “incl­usive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue”. Araghchi also said, “Either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together,” adding that Iran was willing to cooperate with its neighbours. Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis’ recent escalation, a charge Tehran denies. The fighting continued on Saturday, with Saudi Arabia saying it intercepted four drones over Riyadh, the Eastern Province and the south. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said the drones were “intercepted and destroyed” as the kingdom faced repeated Houthi missile and drone attacks on oil installations, tankers and airports. Houthi-affiliated med­ia, meanwhile, said Saudi air strikes beginning overnight killed at least 12 people in Yemen, including three children. It said strikes on “civilian homes” in Taiz killed nine people and wounded 16, while attacks in Dhamar killed three children and wounded 17. The Houthi news agency also alleged that Saudi forces used cluster bombs. The Saudi-led coalition did not immediately comment on that claim. The renewed war in Yemen has intensified since July. The Houthis have attacked Saudi energy facilities, vessels and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed last week. The Houthis have also seized territory around the Bab al-Mandab Strait, increasing pressure on Red Sea shipping and energy exports. Separately, the Houthis announced the release of 159 pro-government fighters under an amnesty after their recent territorial gains. The International Committee of the Red Cross confirmed the release and said it helped with interviews, health checks, family contacts and transportation. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Sharifs invoke security fears to defend KP move
items.description: • PM Shehbaz insists govt was ‘compelled’ to impose emergency and governor’s rule • Says Centre exhausted dialogue before taking measures • Nawaz Sharif stresses decision should have been taken earlier • Accuses PTI of using provincial resources for confrontation LAHORE: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sha­rif and PML-N President Nawaz Sharif on Saturday defended the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with the premier saying the federal government had been “compel­led” to take the step over security conce­rns and the elder Sharif arguing that the intervention should have come much earlier. The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The measures were endorsed by parliament this week amid opposition protests. On Saturday, Shehbaz Sharif visited the residence of Rashid Bashir Virk in Gujranwala to offer condolences over the death of his father, former MNA Mahmood Bashir Virk. After recalling the late PML-N lawmaker’s services, the prime minister said the Centre had made a “last attempt” to avoid imposing emergency, referring to rounds of talks held by a joint government-PPP delegation with the opposition. The second round of talks, held on Oct 3 , lasted several hours but ended without a breakthrough. “They had talks with them (PTI) day and night, for 48 hours, and sat with the intention to settle matters from every aspect,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that a draft agreement had been prepared under which the PTI was to call off its protest march. The prime minister said he had held multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional, as well as with his predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur. “In every meeting, I tried my best to convey to him from the depths of my heart and with seriousness that KP is an extremely beautiful province and has very brave and honourable people, […] and I am always present in every way for their development and prosperity,” the premier said. PM Shehbaz said he had assured the KP government of the Centre’s support in jointly fighting terrorism and addressing security challenges in the province. He added that he had assured the chief minister that decisions regarding administration, resources and requirements would be made in consultation with the provincial government. “But, unfortunately, despite all these efforts, thousands of our law enforcement personnel, soldiers and officers of the armed forces were sacrificing their lives to defend the homeland,” he said. The prime minister said the federal government had made repeated efforts to address the situation but had instead faced “threats and long marches every other day”. The Oct 11 measures followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and PTI, as well as negotiations aimed at bridging differences after the party announced a long march towards Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Nawaz backs governor’s rule Meanwhile, PML-N President Nawaz Sharif on Saturday fully backed the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, saying the measures should have been taken much earlier as the law and order situation deteriorated. Speaking to journalists at his residence in London, Mr Sharif said the situation in KP had become increasingly alarming under the PTI government and that the federal authorities should have intervened before matters worsened further. “This intervention was necessary to restore peace, improve governance and protect the interests of the people,” the former prime minister was quoted as saying by journalist Azhar Javed, who was present in the media talk. Mr Sharif also accused the PTI of using provincial government resources for political confrontation with the federation. “Which country allows a chief minister to use official resources to attack the federal capital?” he asked, questioning the use of provincial resources for political purposes. He accused PTI of damaging the province during its 13 years in power, alleging that successive PTI governments had failed to provide effective governance and neglected the interests of ordinary citizens. Mr Sharif said the people of KP were patriotic Pakistanis who deserved better governance and leadership. Zulqernain Tahir also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Le JZN de Rabat accueille de nouveaux reptiles et amphibiens africains
items.description: Le Jardin Zoologique National (JZN) de Rabat a accueilli 72 nouveaux spécimens représentant 21 espèces de reptiles et d’amphibiens africains, venant enrichir les expositions du Vivarium et élargir la diversité des espèces présentées au public. Parmi les nouveaux pensionnaires figurent notamment le Varan du Nil (Varanus niloticus), le Python d’Anchieta (Python anchietae), le Caméléon panthère (Furcifer pardalis), la Grenouille- taureau africaine (Pyxicephalus adspersus) et le Gecko diurne géant de Madagascar (Phelsuma grandis). Ces espèces témoignent de la remarquable diversité des formes et des modes de vie développés par les reptiles et les amphibiens à travers le continent africain. Ils offrent ainsi l’occasion de mettre en lumière des animaux très diversifiés : prédateurs terrestres et aquatiques, espèces arboricoles, reptiles désertiques ou amphibiens liés aux milieux humides. Chacun présente des adaptations singulières à son environnement, qu’il s’agisse de camouflage, de thermorégulation, de locomotion, de stratégies de chasse ou de reproduction. Avec ces nouveaux spécimens, le Vivarium poursuit sa vocation de faire découvrir une biodiversité africaine d’une grande richesse, et de donner à voir toute la diversité des espèces et des habitats qui la caractérisent. Pour rappel, le Maroc possède une remarquable diversité de reptiles et d’amphibiens. De la Méditerranée au Sahara, en passant par les montagnes, les plaines et les zones humides, la variété des milieux naturels du Royaume accueille une faune herpétologique riche, comprenant notamment plusieurs espèces endémiques. Le Vivarium permet de lui donner une place particulière et de l’inscrire dans une lecture plus large de la diversité de la faune africaine. Inauguré en 2019, le Vivarium s’étend sur près de 1 700 m² et propose un parcours consacré aux reptiles et aux amphibiens à travers six grandes zones biogéographiques : marocaine, subtropicale, afro-alpine, sud-saharienne, équatoriale et malgache. Cette diversité permet de faire découvrir des espèces parfois discrètes ou méconnues, mais qui occupent des fonctions essentielles dans les écosystèmes. Prédateurs, proies ou espèces indicatrices de l’état des milieux, reptiles et amphibiens participent à des équilibres écologiques souvent invisibles. C’est toute la vocation de l’éducation à l’environnement : partir de l’observation pour susciter la connaissance, puis une meilleure compréhension des enjeux de conservation. Cette approche permet également de déconstruire certaines perceptions et idées reçues qui entourent les reptiles et les amphibiens, et de faire découvrir au public des animaux dont la discrétion ne diminue en rien l’importance écologique. Les nouveaux pensionnaires sont passés par une période de quarantaine, sous la supervision des équipes vétérinaires et zoologiques du Jardin Zoologique National. Cette période a permis d’assurer leur suivi sanitaire, d’observer leur comportement et de préparer leur acclimatation pour leur installation progressive dans les espaces du Vivarium.
