items.title: Government appoints AI focal persons across ministries to drive national strategy
items.description: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George, has disclosed that the government has appointed artificial intelligence (AI) focal persons across all ministries as part of efforts to prepare public institutions for the adoption of the technology. He says Cabinet ministers have already undergone AI training, while preparations are underway to equip senior civil servants with the skills needed to integrate artificial intelligence into government operations. “We’ve done the AI boot camp for cabinet ministers. We have AI-focal persons in every ministry now,” he revealed. Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum, Mr George explained that the government is taking steps to ensure that ministries, departments and agencies develop the capacity to deploy AI responsibly and effectively. He disclosed that Ghana has also undertaken an AI readiness assessment in collaboration with UNESCO to determine how prepared government institutions are to adopt the technology. “Working with UNESCO, we’ve done an AI readiness assessment model that has mapped out all of the government ministries and agencies and determined the various states of readiness for our various agencies,” he explained. According to the minister, the findings will help the government identify institutions requiring additional investment, technical support and capacity-building before introducing AI into their operations. He said the assessment would also guide engagements between his ministry and the Ministry of Finance on the resources needed to address gaps in institutional preparedness. The initiative forms part of Ghana’s broader national AI strategy, which seeks to harness the technology to improve economic productivity, strengthen public services and expand access to essential services. The country’s preparedness for artificial intelligence, its impact on jobs and the opportunities for economic growth will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?” The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel , will feature Sam George; Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons. It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m. Training senior public officials Beyond the appointment of AI focal persons, Mr George disclosed that the government is working with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and UNESCO to train senior civil servants, including chief directors and directors across public institutions. “We’re beginning the training, working with the UNDP and UNESCO, for our civil servants, our chief director and director levels,” he said. The training is intended to equip public officials with the knowledge required to understand and apply artificial intelligence within their respective institutions. Mr George believes preparing the public sector is essential because the successful implementation of Ghana’s AI strategy will depend not only on investment in technology but also on the ability of government officials to use it effectively. He explained that Ghana’s AI strategy provides a ten-year development framework with measurable objectives intended to guide the country’s adoption of the technology. “Our AI strategy gives us a 10-year plan of what we intend to achieve, measurable plans of what we need to achieve. We’ve started work on that,” he stated. The strategy identifies agriculture, healthcare, education and government services as priority areas where artificial intelligence could improve productivity and the delivery of essential services. AI to improve government decision-making The sector minister believes artificial intelligence could significantly improve how government institutions plan development projects and allocate public resources. He disclosed that the ministry is developing a national data exchange hub intended to connect 48 data registries across government institutions. The proposed system would allow information currently held in separate databases to be analysed collectively, helping policymakers identify development priorities using empirical evidence. The minister argued that decisions about public investments should be guided by the actual needs of communities rather than political promises or the preferences of influential individuals. “I think that where we should get to as a country is that our interventions in communities must be driven by hardcore empirical evidence,” he said. He explained that data from hospitals, schools and other public institutions could help determine where resources would have the greatest impact. The minister also outlined plans for a national AI compute centre, which he believes will provide the processing infrastructure required to analyse large volumes of government data and support AI applications across different sectors. According to him, the government has committed US$250 million towards the first phase of the project, which is being designed with capacity beyond Ghana’s immediate requirements. Mr George believes combining such infrastructure with improved institutional readiness could enable the government to deliver more efficient and responsive public services. Building a digitally inclusive government Despite the opportunities presented by artificial intelligence, the minister acknowledged that its successful adoption would require sustained investment in infrastructure, cybersecurity, data protection and human capacity. He disclosed that the government is reviewing Ghana’s cybersecurity and data protection legislation to respond to risks associated with the increasing use of AI and large volumes of personal data. Mr George said the objective is to ensure that Ghana takes advantage of emerging technologies while protecting citizens and strengthening the institutions responsible for delivering public services. He expressed optimism that the implementation of the national AI strategy would ultimately help create a more responsive public sector, where citizens can access government services with greater ease. Describing his vision for Ghana’s AI-powered future, the minister said he wants to see “a harmonised system that works for the benefit of the Ghanaian people.” For him, the appointments, training programmes and planned infrastructure investments are steps towards a broader transformation of the Ghanaian economy.

items.title: Ghana needs AI engineers and data scientists, not just computing infrastructure – Hubtel CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Hubtel , Alex Bram, has urged the government to match its planned investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure with funding for specialised training, warning that Ghana’s shortage of skilled professionals could undermine efforts to develop a competitive AI industry. He believes investment in computing infrastructure alone will not be sufficient to drive the country’s AI ambitions without the engineers, data scientists and technical personnel needed to develop, operate and maintain such systems. Mr Bram says Ghana must pay particular attention to building expertise in machine learning, data science and data centre management as it prepares to establish a national AI compute centre. “The money is extremely important. The money to set up the starting data centres and the architecture and the infrastructure around it is very important. But whilst we do that, I think we also have to look at the skills,” he said. Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum, Mr Bram drew on Hubtel ‘s own experience to explain why developing the country’s technical workforce must be treated as a priority alongside investment in physical infrastructure. He disclosed that the company struggled to recruit qualified machine learning engineers when it began developing its own AI systems, despite offering attractive employment packages. The challenge, he believes, exposes a skills gap Ghana must address if it intends to compete in the rapidly expanding global AI economy. The availability of specialised skills, investment in AI infrastructure and the implications of the technology for Ghana’s workforce will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?” The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel , will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George; Economist and Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons. It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m. Hubtel struggled to recruit 30 AI engineers Mr Bram revealed that Hubtel began experimenting with artificial intelligence in 2022 before establishing an AI laboratory in 2023 to develop its own models. The company initially sought to build AI systems using machine learning and neural network technologies, with the ambition of developing solutions tailored to local business needs. However, the initiative encountered difficulties when Hubtel attempted to recruit the technical professionals required to undertake the work. “One, we struggled with manpower. So when we started, we wanted to recruit, I believe it was about 30 machine learning engineers. We just couldn’t find 30 in Ghana,” he disclosed. According to him, the company increased its recruitment budget substantially in an attempt to attract qualified professionals, but the effort yielded limited results. “We increased the budget almost twice, and we still couldn’t find machine learning data scientists who were from Ghana. We offered very generous terms. We still couldn’t find, so our tech was a bit behind,” he explained. Mr Bram said the difficulties affected Hubtel’s ability to advance its own AI technology at a time when international companies were rapidly developing and commercialising more sophisticated systems. By late 2024 and into 2025, commercially available AI models had become considerably more advanced and affordable, making it increasingly difficult for Hubtel to justify continuing along its original development path. The company eventually moved away from building its own models from scratch towards adopting commercially available AI technologies. For Mr Bram, the experience highlights the challenge Ghanaian technology companies could face without a larger pool of trained AI specialists. Beyond the proposed AI compute centre The government’s national AI strategy includes plans to establish an AI compute centre intended to provide the computing capacity required to support the development and deployment of artificial intelligence applications. Communications Minister Sam George has disclosed that the government has committed US$250 million towards the first phase of the facility, alongside US$20 million for a proposed AI fund. Mr Bram welcomed the initiative, describing Ghana’s decision to develop an AI policy framework and invest in infrastructure as an important step. However, he maintained that the country must also develop the specialised human resources required to make the investment productive. “As a country, we haven’t been strong at having a large base of, for example, people that can manage data centres. There are so few data centres here. I think that number needs to go up a little bit. There’s also the skills required to build it,” he observed. He identified machine learning and data science as areas requiring greater investment in technical capacity. “Machine learning, data scientists. We need those skills. And I think we might have to improve our efforts on getting the skills,” he said. Data availability another challenge Beyond the shortage of skilled professionals, Mr Bram identified access to data as another obstacle Hubtel encountered in its attempts to develop AI systems locally. He explained that the company approached other large businesses to explore data-sharing arrangements but struggled because there was no clear framework governing how the information could be exchanged. “We realised there’s still no framework in Ghana for sharing data,” he said. According to him, the uncertainty made companies reluctant to share information, limiting Hubtel’s ability to obtain the data required to improve its AI models. He consequently urged the government to develop arrangements that would encourage the retention and appropriate sharing of useful data to support AI development. “So that data framework is important. If that AI compute centre is to succeed, because when a computer centre is there, without the data, it’s nothing,” he stressed. Mr Bram believes Ghana must therefore address three interconnected requirements: computing infrastructure, access to data and the availability of skilled professionals. Ghana has an opportunity to get it right Despite the challenges Hubtel encountered, Mr Bram remains optimistic about Ghana’s prospects in artificial intelligence. He believes the government’s decision to develop a national strategy and commit resources to the sector provides an opportunity to address existing gaps before they become greater obstacles. The Hubtel CEO wants deliberate investment in technical skills to extend beyond the development of national infrastructure to support the adoption of AI by businesses of different sizes. “I think Ghana is well on the path. I mean, starting with the policy building, putting some money where the policy is heading towards, investing deliberately in the skills, the digital skills required to manage and build and translate and take this AI out to, or this new technology out to everybody else, mass enterprises, micro enterprises and all that. I think we’re already on the path and that’s critical,” he indicated. He argued that training the workforce would be essential to ensuring that the benefits of the technology reach smaller enterprises and other productive sectors of the economy.

items.title: Trunk sellers count losses as SHS students embrace suitcases
items.description: Locally made metal trunk sellers in Accra say their businesses are going through a difficult period as more senior high school (SHS) students opt for suitcases, leaving traders with unsold stock. The sellers, some of whom have been in the trade for decades, attribute the decline in demand for trunks to changing consumer preferences, the inclusion of suitcases on school prospectuses and the sale of school supplies on campuses. A trunk seller, who has been in the business for about 10 years, Mr Victor Amankwa, said this year’s sales had been particularly poor for him, with only 20 trunks sold, compared to more than 50 in previous years. He said a medium-sized trunk sold for GH¢200, the same price as a traditional chop box. According to him, many young people now consider metal trunks old-fashioned and prefer suitcases, which they perceive as more modern and easier to transport on wheels. “We have not had any bad feedback on the use of trunks. Suitcases get spoilt easily. The trunk is the best. If they are taking out anything or a chop box, they should make the trunk compulsory,” he suggested. He cited Presbyterian Boys’ Senior High School (PRESEC) and Achimota School as institutions that still accepted trunks. Mr Amankwa said parents could also save money by keeping trunks for younger siblings rather than purchasing new suitcases for every child. “They forget that the trunk can be used by the younger ones coming. Parents do not have to waste money buying another one. They only need to clean and spray it for about GH¢15,” he said. He argued that listing suitcases alongside trunks on school prospectuses was contributing to the decline in demand and called for a review of the practice. Local production under threat Another trunk seller, Mr Peter Anderson, said the decline in demand was affecting a trade that supported local manufacturing, particularly in the Bukom area in Accra. He said he previously sold more than 50 trunks whenever first-year students were preparing to enter school, in addition to bulk purchases by other traders. However, he said some of his regular wholesale buyers now purchased only five or 10 pieces because sales had dropped. Mr Anderson said traders and producers had been left with large quantities of unsold trunks in their warehouses, raising concerns about the money invested in their production. He urged school authorities to reconsider the inclusion of suitcases on school prospectuses, arguing that trunks remained a durable and reusable option for students. “For wooden chop boxes, we understand when they say they generate bedbugs in the school. What about trunks?” he asked. Mr Kobby Frimps, another trunk seller, blamed school authorities for allowing the sale of school supplies on their campuses. Plastic chop boxes are replacing traditional wooden ones on SHS prospectuses to prevent bed bug infestation He said parents who would otherwise purchase the items from market traders were increasingly buying them directly from school-based shops. He expressed concern about the cost of plastic chop boxes, noting that prices and quality varied between the locally made ones and the imported ones. He said some imported boxes had durable bodies but weaker covers, while local versions had more durable covers, and advised parents to examine the products carefully before buying. School requirements and traders’ concerns Madam Serwaa Ampaafo, who has sold trunks and other school items for 34 years, said interventions by some Members of Parliament (MPs), who allegedly supplied trunks and chop boxes to schools for distribution to students, were also affecting market sales. She argued that such assistance could instead be given directly to parents, allowing them to buy the required items from traders. “And so, because of this, they did not come to the market to buy. How can they do this to our business? How do they expect us to make sales?” she asked. During a visit to Accra Girls’ Senior High School, The Mirror saw a shop selling school supplies, including plastic chop boxes. Some parents who arrived with wooden chop boxes were reportedly asked to take them back and purchase plastic alternatives costing about GH¢350. There were suitcases in several dormitories visited. Suitcase sellers also feel the pinch However, suitcase sellers told The Mirror that the change in students’ preferences had not necessarily translated into sustained sales for them. At the Okaishie Market in Accra, a suitcase seller, Mr Samuel Osae, said the period of brisk sales lasted only about two weeks this year, compared with the one or two months of brisk business he experienced in previous years. He attributed the situation partly to the high cost of preparing children for school, particularly the purchase of plastic chop boxes. He said some parents who spent about GH¢650 on a better-quality plastic chop box could no longer afford a suitcase. Mr Osae said a single suitcase sold for about GH¢350, while a set of three cost between GH¢600 and GH¢700.

items.title: Pakistan suspends Iran trade corridors over 'security, smuggling concerns'
items.description: GWADAR/QUETTA: Pakistan has suspended trade with Iran through the official Gabd-Rimdan (250) and Taftan border crossings, it emerged on Saturday. The Ministry of Commerce issued a memorandum on Friday, seen by Dawn , withdrawing its earlier order [No. 9(3)2017-Iran] dated Oct 3 with immediate effect. Shahid Rind, adviser to the Balochistan chief minister on media and political affairs, said the “purpose of the temporary closure of the Pak-Iran border is to address security concerns, prevent smuggling, and make the border system more effective”. In a statement on X, Rind refuted “rumours being spread on social media” regarding the closure and urged the public not to pay attention to unverified information. The Balochistan official stressed that the move was “necessary to improve the security situation and administrative affairs on both sides of the border”. Rind affirmed that “progress continues between the high officials of both countries to resolve administrative issues” related to the border. “In the context of the current progress, the Pak-Iran border is likely to reopen soon,” he said, adding that a coordinated system was being established to improve border affairs and prevent smuggling. Meanwhile, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei also said the closure was temporary, Iran’s state-run Irna reported . However, he attributed the move to “technical issues” and said the two countries were in consultations to resolve the problem and restore normal operations. Separately, the Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry (QCCI) has also advised its members and businesses involved in trade with Iran to stop placing new import and export orders until further notice. Sources said Pakistani and Iranian authorities had made initial contact following the closure. Hundreds of freight vehicles carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), rice, fresh fruit and other essential commodities have reportedly been stranded on both sides of the border. According to Iran-based Wana news agency, passenger traffic through the Rimdan–Gabd crossing remains operational. It quoted Syed Hossein Hosseini, director general of the Iranian Transit Office, as saying that commercial operations at the border crossing had been halted. The Gabd-Rimdan crossing had become a major route for meeting Pakistan’s energy needs, with over 4,000 tonnes of LPG reportedly imported daily through it. Exports of Pakistani products, particularly rice, had also surged in recent months, generating millions of dollars in foreign exchange. Sources in the trade and energy sector warned that the closure could aggravate LPG shortages in Karachi and other parts of the country. The Taftan route was already facing disruptions amid unrest in Balochistan. The suspension of supplies through Gabd-Rimdan could push up LPG prices in the open market. Local traders and the chamber have warned that the disruption could cause not only substantial losses to the national exchequer and jeopardise the livelihoods of many but also an energy crisis. Since March this year, Islamabad and Tehran have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures , formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes , against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran war that has strained economies in the region and beyond. In early August, an Iranian delegation led by Trade and Industry Minister Mohammad Atabak visited Islamabad for the 10th session of the Pak–Iran Joint Trade Committee (JTC). The delegation also met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, with both sides agreeing to further expand trade ties by keeping border crossings open round the clock, improving logistics and harmonising customs procedures. The visit came a couple of months after it was reported that trade between Pakistan and Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing had come to a complete halt. According to Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry President Jiand Hoot, trade through the Panjgur and Mand-Radig border crossings was virtually non-existent because of poor road infrastructure and recurring incidents of arson and vehicle burnings.

items.title: A proper reset would’ve been to clear the EC and set new standards – Suhuyini on EC appointments
items.description: Deputy Minister for Roads and Highways Alhassan Suhuyini says a proper reset of Ghana’s Electoral Commission (EC) would have involved replacing the existing commissioners and establishing a transparent process for appointing people with proven integrity and credibility without partisan biases. He argued that such a process would help restore public confidence in the Commission by ensuring that those appointed to oversee the country’s electoral processes are perceived as impartial and independent of political parties. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 17, Mr Suhuyini said the President should have been allowed to start afresh by clearing the Commission and working towards a new framework for selecting its leadership. “I’m saying that the proper reset, in my view, would have been if the President had the opportunity to wipe the slate clean and then institutionalise a process that will allow for the appointment of people that we can all have confidence in,” he said. He stressed that the appointment process should prioritise individuals with established records of integrity and credibility, without obvious affiliations with political parties. “A process, I’m sure, can bring about that. That would have been a proper reset,” he added. He maintained that such an approach would have provided an opportunity to build a system that commands broader public confidence, rather than relying solely on appointments made within the existing arrangements. “Wipe the slate clean. Clear all those politically affiliated people ex-President Akufo-Addo packed that place with, that would have been an ideal reset,” he said. He argued that a proper reset would have required the removal of commissioners appointed under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo’s administration, followed by a national discussion on how their replacements should be selected. “Take them all out and then let’s together as a nation, sit down and discuss how we want people who are commissioners appointed. That would have been the appropriate thing,” he said. However, he noted that the laws governing the Electoral Commission constrain the President’s ability to remove the commissioners, while such a move could also attract concerns from the international community. “We all know that the laws will not allow him to do that easily. We know that the international community will raise eyebrows about the removal of these people,” he said. Against that background, Mr Suhuyini acknowledged that the government had to work within the existing legal framework, particularly given that two vacancies had arisen on the Commission. He said the existence of those vacancies formed part of the considerations surrounding the current appointment discussions, although he clarified that his position should not be interpreted as an endorsement of any particular appointment decision. His comments come amid discussions about appointments to the Electoral Commission and the need to ensure that the institution is trusted by political parties and the wider public. The Commission is responsible for organising and supervising public elections in Ghana, making its perceived independence and neutrality central to confidence in the country’s democratic process. Mr Suhuyini’s position is that, beyond filling existing vacancies, the country should consider how appointments to the Commission can be structured to strengthen public confidence in the institution and reduce concerns about partisan influence.

items.title: Entre la CEDEAO et l’AES, les premiers ponts se construisent à Dakar
items.description: La Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO) et la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) ont tenu à Dakar la première session de leur dialogue ministériel sur la coopération. Les deux organisations ont convenu de créer des groupes de travail conjoints, dont les travaux doivent aboutir à un accord-cadre. La délégation de la CEDEAO était conduite par Cheikh Niang, ministre sénégalais de l'Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l'Extérieur, qui préside aussi le Conseil des ministres de l'organisation. Côté AES, la délégation avait à sa tête Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré, ministre burkinabè des Affaires étrangères et président du Comité ministériel de pilotage de la Confédération. Les deux hommes ont coprésidé la réunion. Le communiqué conjoint, publié ce 17 octobre 2026, décrit une rencontre de « prise de contact et d'échanges » destinée à « poser les bases » de la coopération. Les deux parties y saluent « l'esprit de fraternité, de respect mutuel et d'ouverture » qui a marqué leurs discussions et rappellent les liens historiques, socioculturels et économiques entre leurs peuples. Le texte fixe d'abord le cadre politique. Les relations devront être guidées par le « bon voisinage », le respect de la souveraineté, de la dignité et du bien-être des populations ouest-africaines. Les deux organisations affichent la volonté de parvenir à « un cadre de coopération équilibré, réaliste » qui préserve les intérêts des peuples. Le communiqué ne détaille pas les domaines de coopération. Il indique seulement que les parties ont échangé sur les sujets « d'intérêt commun » autour desquels les prochaines discussions pourront être structurées, sans les nommer. Il situe cette rencontre dans le prolongement de leurs consultations du 22 mai 2025 à Bamako, au Mali. La suite : des groupes de travail La décision concrète est la mise en place de « groupes de travail thématiques conjoints », chargés des échanges techniques. Leur but est la conclusion d'un « accord-cadre de coopération » entre la CEDEAO et la Confédération AES. Leurs résultats seront soumis aux ministres avant la prochaine session. Le calendrier reste ouvert : la date et le lieu de cette prochaine réunion seront fixés après consultation « par voie diplomatique ». Le communiqué ne mentionne ni composition des groupes ni échéance pour l'accord. Les deux parties ont exprimé leur gratitude au président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, président en exercice de la Conférence des chefs d'État et de gouvernement de la CEDEAO, ainsi qu'au gouvernement et au peuple sénégalais pour leur hospitalité. O.B.N

items.title: Malang Sarr : « Les ambitions et les objectifs sont aussi hauts que les supporters sénégalais »
items.description: Victoire, cage inviolée, premiers pas en Tanière : Malang Sarr a réussi ses débuts avec le Sénégal le 29 septembre, en Éthiopie. Dans un entretien accordé aux médias de la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF), le défenseur raconte son intégration, son père, qui l'a mené jusqu'ici, mais aussi les ambitions avec la Tanière. À Bahir Dar, à 1 800 mètres d'altitude, l'hymne national résonne. Malang Sarr ferme les yeux. Pour sa première sélection, ce sont d'abord les siens qu'il porte avec lui, et surtout un père parti trop tôt, qui vivait ce rêve à travers lui. Dans un entretien accordé aux médias de la FSF, le défenseur se livre à cœur ouvert. Lorsque l’hymne national a retenti lors de sa première sélection, l’ancien Lensois a eu des flash-back. « Tout se mélange. J’ai mes souvenirs personnels de l’équipe nationale. Quand on était en famille et qu’il y avait un match de l’équipe nationale à la télé, on était tous en famille au salon. Je pense forcément à mon père, à mes parents, à ma famille entière, parce que ce n’est pas seulement moi qui réalise mon rêve, mais le fait d’avoir mon nom sur le maillot, c’est toute ma famille qui est représentée. C’est fort. Je ne pense pas qu’on puisse décrire cela. On peut jouer pour un club, porter des maillots, mais porter le maillot de l’équipe nationale, c’est quelque chose qui est à part. Ça n’a rien à voir. Trouver des mots pour décrire ça, je ne pense pas que je puisse le faire, c’est vraiment de la fierté. C’est un honneur parce qu’on est choisi. On est 23, on est 26, on est 30. Parmi les 20 millions de Sénégalais, voire plus, qui rêveraient de représenter le pays. Il faut être à la hauteur. On est juste bénis et honorés d’être dans cette position-là. » Ce soir-là, le Sénégal s'impose sans encaisser de but. Pour le défenseur, c'est le début d'une nouvelle histoire. À 27 ans, Malang Sarr n’est plus un débutant. Avec son expérience (Nice, Chelsea, Lens notamment), le défenseur central a connu divers vestiaires. Par ailleurs, le groupe Sénégal a aussi facilité son intégration. « Bien sûr, le message est passé, il est très clair. Les cadres ont été vraiment clairs et je suis reconnaissant parce que je ressens vraiment le rôle qu’ils veulent me donner, malgré ce qui vient d’arriver et la considération qu’ils ont pour moi aussi, parce que si je n’étais pas en mesure de le faire, ils ne m’auraient pas passé le message. L’idée est vraiment claire, c’est d’expliquer le fonctionnement du groupe, comment le groupe fonctionne, comment la fédération fonctionne, l’équipe nationale fonctionne, vraiment de me donner le maximum de clés possibles, leur donner aussi mon avis sur comment je fonctionnerais pour aider le groupe de la meilleure des manières. C’est simplement des discussions pour ajouter les meilleurs détails possibles pour être le plus efficace pour le groupe. Je suis vraiment content, si demain je suis amené à jouer un de ces rôles-là, de me donner à fond et d’aider l’équipe nationale de la meilleure des manières. » Portrait-robot Lors de cet entretien avec la Fédération sénégalaise de football, Malang Sarr en a profité pour décliner son identité footballistique, histoire de se présenter à ceux qui ne le connaissent pas vraiment. « Aujourd’hui, quand les gens parlent de moi, en général, c’est ma vitesse. Pour un défenseur, c’est quelque chose d’important. Ma vitesse, ma qualité de relance, mon aisance dans le duel 1 contre 1. Je pense que ce sont des qualités qui sont importantes chez un joueur. De pouvoir être dur dans le duel, de pouvoir relancer correctement, de pouvoir avoir la vitesse. Parce qu’aujourd’hui, tous les attaquants vont vite, tous les joueurs sont rapides, le football change aussi. Tout ce qui fait d’un défenseur, toutes les qualités qu’il faut avoir pour un défenseur, j’essaie d’en avoir quelques-unes. Si je ne les ai pas, je travaille tous les jours pour les améliorer », débute-t-il. Et le néo-Lion de poursuivre. « Je dirais rapide, à l’aise dans la relance, forcément, et à l’aise dans les duels aussi. J’essaie d’être meilleur chaque jour et j’arrive dans une période de ma carrière où je me connais bien. J’ai vécu de belles expériences, que ce soit bonnes ou mauvaises, mais qui m’ont forgé. Aujourd’hui, j’arrive au meilleur moment de ma carrière et je joue mon meilleur football, je pense. » En outre, Malang Sarr a laissé un message aux supporters sénégalais, qui sont réputés être d’une grande exigence, notamment après avoir remporté deux des trois dernières CAN. « Les ambitions et les objectifs sont aussi hauts que les supporters sénégalais. On a vraiment l’ambition et l’intention de donner du plaisir par le jeu et surtout de donner du plaisir par la victoire, parce qu’aujourd’hui, c’est ce qu’on retient. Les victoires, les trophées, les succès, ce sont des choses qui restent. Donc, on va faire le maximum pour faire plaisir aux Sénégalais, parce que les Sénégalais aiment le beau jeu. Ils aiment aussi des joueurs qui se battent, qui se donnent à fond. Et je pense que de commencer par ça, se donner à fond, donner le meilleur de nous-mêmes, déjà, on sera capables de conquérir le peuple sénégalais à nouveau. Mais il y a une période de transition qui est en place. On ambitionne d’être à la hauteur et d’être au même niveau que ce qui s’est fait précédemment. Aujourd’hui, je pense qu’on est sur la bonne voie. On a tous les outils et toutes les armes pour y arriver. Je tiens à dire au peuple sénégalais qu’on va se donner à fond pour le rendre fier et pour atteindre les objectifs que l’on s’est fixés, c’est-à-dire de gagner encore des trophées et d’être à la hauteur. » O.B.N

items.title: France : scènes de chaos en marge de manifestations contre la vie chère
items.description: Mairies incendiées, préfectures attaquées, des rues et des magasins dévastés : en France, les manifestations contre la vie chère ont été émaillées de violences ce samedi 17 octobre. Quelque 800 000 personnes sont sorties à l’appel de plusieurs organisations syndicales et des partis de gauche après une semaine de mobilisation des lycéens contre le manque de moyens dans les lycées. Cette journée de colère a été marquée par des scènes de chaos et de pillage à Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Limoges. Emmanuel Grégoire, le maire socialiste de la capitale français évoque des « rues entières » qui ont été « méthodiquement ravagées ». Le bilan des violences et pillages commis samedi à Paris serait « lourd » et « d'ampleur immense ». À France Info, il a fait état de « dégâts sur l'espace public et des monuments qui ont été dégradés, cassés ». La situation est totalement hors de contrôle à Paris dans le secteur République. Des dizaines de boutiques sont pillées depuis plus de deux heures sur le boulevard Magenta. #Paris #17octobre https://t.co/iV95XdDyby — Luc Auffret (@LucAuffret) October 17, 2026 Le maire de Marseille Benoît Payan réclame des comptes À Marseille, les violences ont touché des édifices publics et des magasins. « Le poste de police municipale de la Canebière a été vandalisé, les portes de l’Hôtel de Ville ont été forcées, de nombreux commerces ont été dégradés », a écrit le maire de la deuxième plus grande ville de France, le socialiste Benoît Payan, en faisant état d’une situation « hors de contrôle » dans le centre-ville de Marseille dans la matinée de ce samedi. Marseille : plusieurs dizaines de manifestants ont pénétré brièvement samedi dans le hall de la mairie, sur le vieux port, après avoir enfoncé la porte en criant « c'est la Révolution, on prend la Bastille ». Ils ont été dispersés par des forces de l'ordre https://t.co/QMtEYxYZTK — Agence France-Presse (@afpfr) October 17, 2026 « Les manifestants ne sont pas des casseurs. Les casseurs, je veux qu'ils soient en prison. Je veux savoir ce qui s’est passé, je ne me tairai pas. Je veux savoir pourquoi dans cette ville, des gens ont pu impunément casser », a-t-il déclaré à BFMTV. Manifestations du 17 octobre: « Les casseurs, je veux qu'ils soient en prison », assène Benoît Payan, maire de Marseille après une intrusion dans l'Hôtel de Ville https://t.co/JP3mR3t7Ro — BFM (@BFMTV) October 17, 2026 Le président Emmanuel Macron a réagi en mettant en garde les casseurs. « Aucune place pour la violence dans notre République. Ceux qui ont cassé, attaqué les préfectures comme les commerces, pillé jusqu’à nos mairies, seront poursuivis et punis », a-t-il écrit. items.description: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, WTO, has recalled how her investigation into an alleged $2.4bn fuel subsidy fraud in Nigeria led her mother’s kidnapping. Read Also: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother, 82, kidnapped Okonjo-Iweala narrated her experience in an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua. She said the kidnappers’ demands were that she resigns as the Minister of Finance and leave the country. On how the ordeal began, she said her office noticed a sharp increase in subsidy claims, so she began to probe. Her words: “So I went to the president and said, look, something is going on here. Could we audit the accounts? And he said, yes, go ahead. “And we found about $2.4 billion worth of fraud. So we refused to pay.” That was when they took her mother. Okonjo-Iweala said the five-day ordeal was among the most painful periods of her life. “I was told (by the kidnappers) that for her to be released, I should resign and leave the country. “She was held in the middle of a forest, and one night she escaped. She’s still alive. She’s 96 now.” “It was a terrible, terrible five-day ordeal. I think the worst in my life,” she said. Okonjo-Iweala said initially she felt paralysed by fear and considered resigning. She added that that the experience left her with a sense of guilt that she still carries. “I never dreamt my parents could ever be touched in this way, that people would be that evil,” she said. On her father’s reaction at the time, she said: “He said, ‘We don’t give in to blackmail’. And he said, ‘You’ve got to carry on. You’ve got to go to work’.” Okonjo-Iweala served as Minister of Finance under President Goodluck Jonathan. Her mother, Kamene Okonjo, was kidnapped from her home in Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, in December 2012. Read the kidnap story HERE . items.title: Zulum calls for coordinated military offensive in the Lake Chad
items.description: …Zulum’s support instrumental to military success – COAS By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has called on the military to immediately commence a coordinated offensive operation, Operation Lake Sanity, to dislodge insurgents from the shores and islands of Lake Chad. Governor Zulum made the call on Saturday when he received the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, on a courtesy visit at the new Council Chamber, Government House, Maiduguri. The governor commended the Nigerian Army for improvements in the security situation in the state and also requested stronger military deployments in strategic locations, including Kareto, Baga, and the Sabon Gari–Wajiroko axis, to protect communities, secure waterways, and support the reopening of the Damboa–Biu road. “The recent attacks on some communities in northern Borno are a result of the presence of insurgents along the shores of Lake Chad. We cannot achieve complete peace without undertaking major military operations in that area,” Zulum said. The governor acknowledged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s support for the proposed operation and the coordination among the service chiefs; however, he urged the military authorities to accelerate preparations. “I understand that the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has provided the necessary support for the operation. I urge you to hasten the process so that the insurgents threatening northern Borno can be dislodged,” he stated. He called for strengthening the amphibious command in Baga to clear waterways, stressing that holding those positions would be essential to sustaining the operation’s gains. On the Gubio–Damasak corridor, Zulum appealed for the speedy establishment of a military formation in Kareto, and around Sabon Gari and Wajiroko in Damboa Local Government Area to support the restoration of vehicular movement between Damboa and Biu. Governor Babagana Zulum thanked the Chief of Army Staff for training about 1,000 forest guards, who he said had completed their training and were deployed to the state. Zulum emphasised the need to consolidate military successes through reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement, commending the Army’s support for re-establishing the Mairari community and preparing for military formations and community resettlement in Maiwa, Koshobe and Ala. “Military operations must be followed by stabilisation measures, including reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement. Borno State Government will provide the support required by the Nigerian Army to fortify these locations,” he pledged. He also expressed appreciation for additional battalions deployed across the two sectors, noting that the reinforcements were helping to strengthen security and stabilise affected areas. “Notwithstanding the recent attacks in some parts of Borno State, there has been tremendous improvement in our security situation. I commend the officers and men of Operation Hadin Kai and urge them to sustain this momentum,” Zulum announced. The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, commended Governor Babagana Umara Zulum for his sustained support to the Nigerian Army, describing it as instrumental to the successes recorded against insurgency. “I must put on record that the support of the Executive Governor of Borno State has been phenomenal in the successes we have recorded here in Borno State. For that, we say a very big thank you, sir,” the COAS said. The Army Chief explained that his visit to troops of Operation Hadin Kai was part of a routine assessment of their operations, to encourage commanders, and to appreciate the resilience of personnel confronting insurgency in the Northeast. He reaffirmed their mandate to restore normalcy and create an enabling environment for socio-economic activities, assuring that challenges presented by commanders would receive prompt attention. The courtesy visit was attended by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, member representing Marte, Monguno, Nganzai federal constituency, Hon. Bukar Talba, Secretary to the State Government, Commissioners, Special Advisers and other senior military and heads of security establishment in the state. End The post Zulum calls for coordinated military offensive in the Lake Chad appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana’s foreign policy will not be dictated by other countries – Ablakwa
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa says Ghana’s pursuit of a partnership with BRICS reflects the independent foreign policy tradition championed by the country’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 17, Mr Ablakwa clarified that President John Dramani Mahama’s administration was seeking partner status with the grouping rather than full membership. He linked the initiative to the spirit of the Non-Aligned Movement, of which Dr Nkrumah was a founding leader, saying the government was reawakening Ghana’s longstanding commitment to an independent voice in international affairs. His explanation placed the historical connection in Ghana’s foreign policy outlook, rather than suggesting that an application to join BRICS began under Dr Nkrumah. “With all due respect, the foreign policy of Ghana will not be dictated by other countries, with all due respect. We cherish the cordial relationship with the United States of America, but Article 40 of our constitution is very clear that our foreign policy consideration must be guided by our national interest,” “Ghana is a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement, which was established in 1961. It was Osagyefo Dr Nkrumah who rallied President Tito, President Abdel Nasser, and the Prime Ministers of India and Indonesia to form the Non-Aligned Movement,” he said. Mr Ablakwa maintained that Ghana’s international partnerships would be guided by its national interests and would not be determined by other countries. His comments followed criticism of the proposed BRICS partnership, including concerns about its potential implications for Ghana’s relations with the United States. The Minister argued that the government should retain the freedom to pursue cooperation that advances the country’s interests.

items.title: Jonathan, Dangote demand jobs, non-kinetic approach to defeat insecurity
items.description: **Urges Revisit of Almajiri Schools for Vulnerable Children. By Kingsley Omonobi Former President Dr Goodluck Jonathan and Africa’s wealthiest man, Aliko Dangote, on Saturday called for greater investment in job creation and social development as part of efforts to tackle terrorism and other forms of insecurity in Nigeria. This is as Jonathan called for a revisit of the Almajiri education system, which he pioneered during his administration to halt the tendency of vulnerable youths being recruited for criminal activities, noting that the Great Green Wall project introduced to keep youths gainfully employed in agriculture should also be revisited. The duo spoke at the public presentation of the book, “Beyond the Bullets: Policing Terrorism in a Democratic System”, written by a former Inspector-General of Police, IGP Mohammed Abubakar. Represented by his former Chief of Staff, Chief Mike Oghiadomhe, Jonathan said the Almajiri schools programme was designed to equip young people with skills beyond religious education and enable them to contribute to national development. “My administration engaged in the establishment of Almajiri schools, aimed at providing skills to millions of youth population beyond religious education only,” he said. Jonathan disclosed that the initiative was intended to help young people earn a living while reducing the number of youths available for recruitment into violent crime. He also said the Great Green Wall project had the potential to address desertification, support agriculture and create employment. “We also engaged in the Great Green Wall project, which, apart from arresting desertification and making more fertile land available for crop farming and animal husbandry, had the potential of providing employment for hundreds of thousands,” he said. While urging the government to revisit both programmes, he added, “I therefore use this opportunity to call on government to revisit and review these programmes.” He said terrorism is a national and global challenge that required sustained commitment and cooperation across successive administrations. His words, “The fight against terrorism is not the responsibility of one administration or the other. It is a continuing national and global challenge that requires sustained commitment, institutional learning, and cooperation across successive governments and generations. In his remarks, Alhaji Aliko Dangote called on the government and private sector to work together to create jobs and stimulate economic growth, arguing that military force alone could not eliminate terrorism. “If you don’t create jobs, it’s difficult to fight terrorism and get it out of the way,” he said. He noted that entrepreneurs had a responsibility to partner with the government by investing in businesses that could generate employment and prosperity. “On our own side as entrepreneurs, we have to partner with the government, create jobs, create growth, and also prosperity, and that will help when they are also fighting with force,” he said. Dangote disclosed that combining economic opportunities with security operations could help Nigeria overcome terrorism, banditry and other forms of violent crime. “If you use these two things, we will get rid of terrorism, banditry, and the rest,” he said. He cited the economic cost of the conflict in the Northeast, saying a UNICEF report put the cumulative national economic loss at about $100bn since the conflict began. “But personally, I believe when you look at the agricultural side of the country and other things, this is more than $100 billion by far. While urging Nigerians to support efforts to address insecurity rather than leave the responsibility to the government alone, he said, “Fighting terrorism is not only for the government alone; it’s our collective responsibility.” “What we need to do is to join hands with the government in fighting this menace, because it is a collective responsibility on all of us.” In his remarks, IGP MD Abubakar said the fight against terrorism must not undermine democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law. Abubakar said the central message of his book was that the fight against terrorism should combine effective security operations with fairness, accountability and respect for human dignity. “This book insists on a vital point that I learned in service. Fighting terrorism should never mean treating the whole community as suspects. He warned that excessive use of power could damage the relationship between security agencies and the communities they were meant to protect. “When fear becomes policy, discrimination becomes security. He stressed that democratic institutions, including the courts, legislature, media and civil society, should not be regarded as obstacles to national security. “They are the ground rails that prevent security from becoming domination,” he said. According to him, “Effective counterterrorism required coordination among security agencies, intelligence gathering, accountability and respect for the law. “Democracies must answer violence with process. He disclosed that justice remained central to democratic security, insisting that investigations must be credible, evidence tested and victims heard. He added that governments needed coordination, security agencies required adequate capability and funding, communities needed trust, courts needed evidence, and citizens deserved transparency. Dignitaries present at the occasion include Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State and Mr Peter Obi, former governor of Anambra State; Dr Bukola Saraki, former Senate President; Inspector General of Police IGP Olatunji Disu; Senator Ireti Kingibe; and Gen Aliyu Gusau, former National Security Adviser, among others. The post Jonathan, Dangote demand jobs, non-kinetic approach to defeat insecurity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: To suggest Anthony Kila hasn’t gone to school is stupid — Utomi
items.description: Political Economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, says he cannot guarantee that embattled professor Anthony Kila has never made mistakes but to suggest that he has never gone to school is spectacularly unfair to his personality. Utomi made this known on his verified Facebook page in Lagos on Saturday, saying that Kila is a good man. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that Kila is currently at the centre of a major scandal regarding his academic credentials. In October, an investigative report published by Premium Times revealed that Kila allegedly falsified all of his higher education qualifications, including his bachelor’s, master’s, doctorate (PhD) degrees, and his rank as a professor. Utomi, reacting to the online claim, said that there was no evidence to support the claim that Anthony Kila (popularly known as “Prof Kila”) had never gone to school. “I know Anthony Kila. I became aware of all the trending discussions about his career rather late. “I have never had any reason to ask about his certificates or letters of appointment, so I cannot claim to have those details. “However, if he has never gone to school, then those who have must ask for a refund. “We watched the cyber mob bully Jason Arday, the youngest Black professor ever appointed at Cambridge, to his early death. “Incidentally, I first met Anthony Kila in the city of Cambridge, England, in 2006, when I was beginning a run for the office of President of Nigeria.” Utomi said that among those in the mob that sought to lynch Arday were white professors, who had been pardoned for mistakes of a far worse nature. He said he did not know who might be going after Kila in a country where many people confer academic and non-academic titles on themselves, while the media, through its status-conferring function, elevates them to celebrity status. He, however, said that this does not seem normal, saying he could empathise because he has had a similar experience. Utomi said: “Years ago, when a journalist tried to suggest that my stay at Volkswagen Nigeria had something to do with its demise, I offered ₦12 million to anyone who could produce a shred of evidence to support that claim. Fifteen years on, no one has come forward to claim the bounty. “When I became the first professor of Pan-African (Pan-Atlantic) parent of the Lagos Business School, someone at UNILAG went, “…huh, until he found out that the evaluating team was led by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan.” “If professors like Adele Jinadu in Political Science and Joe Umo at UNILAG had not met me in graduate school abroad and interacted with my Head of Department, Elinor Lin Ostrom, who went on to become the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, someone may have written something demeaning about my education. “Kila is a smart and good man. I cannot guarantee he has not made mistakes but to suggest he has not gone to school is spectacularly stupid.” (NAN) The post To suggest Anthony Kila hasn’t gone to school is stupid — Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fazl clarifies he criticised policies, not institutions after ministers allege he sought 'share' in KP governance
items.description: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday clarified that his party’s remarks regarding the country’s security situation were directed at policies, not institutions, and termed the allegations levelled against him by federal ministers as character assassination. A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, without naming anyone, had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset” about not being appointed the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The remarks came after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights and raised doubts over its reasoning behind imposing governor’s rule that there was a lack of cooperation on counterterrorism. Earlier on Saturday, State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also rebuked the JUI-F chief for reportedly seeking his “share” in KP’s governance following the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province. Other federal ministers have also taken exception to Fazl’s remarks. Addressing a press conference in Lahore on Saturday, Fazl stressed that his party’s criticism was directed at policies, not institutions, and was intended to bring about corrective action rather than undermine the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism. The senior politician called for an in-camera session of Parliament to review the country’s security situation and formulate a consensus-based policy to combat terrorism. “Our only question is why the country has failed to eliminate terrorism. Let us sit together and find out why. Parliament is the most appropriate forum to discuss the issue and make decisions. Instead of ridiculing politicians, the government should take them on board in this fight so that we can move forward together,” he said. “If Parliament is supreme, why are decisions taken in Rawalpindi while Parliament is simply told to follow them?” he remarked. “The issue is that this government is powerless. Decisions are taken somewhere else, and it implements them obediently,” he alleged. The JUI-F maintained that Parliament should review the security situation and that the nation should be taken into confidence. If the public was expected to support the fight against terrorism and those engaged in it, he argued, the government should explain its decisions rather than impose “unilateral measures”. Fazl reiterated his objection to the imposition of emergency rule in KP or any other part of the country. Recalling his family’s opposition to emergency rule in Balochistan during the 1970s, he said his father had resigned when the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto imposed it in the province. He described the recurrence of such measures as unfortunate, pointing out that the PP had repeatedly been associated with their imposition. Questioning the rationale behind the emergency, governor’s rule and deployment of troops in KP, Fazl asked why the province should face such treatment when Balochistan was also grappling with the same level of terrorist violence, if not more. The JUI-F chief urged the government to develop a shared national narrative and a consensus-based counterterrorism strategy instead of questioning his party’s position. He went on to ask why the government engaged in negotiations with the PTI, which had been in power in KP, if the party was accused of supporting terrorists. “On top of it, both (the PTI and the government) say that they had reached a consensus on all points.” Fazl then highlighted that around 250 of his party workers had lost their lives in terrorist violence, arguing that their sacrifices should not be ridiculed or overlooked. “How can a party whose members have laid their lives be accused of supporting terrorists?” he asked. He also questioned why he was being singled out for criticism when political leaders, including former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, had at various times disagreed with the military leadership. Ministers assail Fazl Earlier on Saturday, addressing the media in Jaranwala, Chaudhry said, “I am upset. We did not expect Maulana sahib […] to consider this as spoils of war and seek his share in the absence of a PTI government in the province.” He emphasised that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was not a political move aimed at strengthening the PML-N’s presence in the province by dismissing the PTI-led government. “This was an administrative setup,” he said, adding that it had been formed with a “one-point agenda: combating terrorism”, rather than with an intention of establishing a political setup. “This is not spoils of war,” he reiterated, adding that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was an “immensely responsible” decision taken after every other option had been considered. “I am unable to understand why Maulana sahab says that he was forced to accept defeat [in elections],” he said, arguing that Fazl’s party had been defeated by the PTI in KP and the Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party in Balochistan. Chaudhry said the JUI-F was worthy of respect only if it stood by Pakistan’s interests. The state minister also rejected the impression that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule was aimed at taking control of KP’s natural resources. He also criticised Fazl for bringing up the 1971 separation of East Pakistan — now Bangladesh — from Pakistan in his recent statements. “You bring up 1971 after losing the 2024 elections,” Chaudhry said. “This KP setup is not about distributing shares, forming coalitions and governments, or engaging in politics,” he stressed, clarifying that only one member of the KP Advisory Council has a political background, as she represents the families of martyrs. Chaudhry again offered to implement the National Action Plan and combat terrorism jointly with all stakeholders. “Politics is possible only where there is peace,” he said. At the outset of his address, Chaudhry alleged that there must be “a relationship or a mutual interest arrangement between the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the PTI”. “Since 2015, no PTI leader, gathering or member has been targeted by terrorists,” Chaudhry said. “On the other hand, over the past 11 years, no political or religious party, security force, public office, funeral or wedding has been spared terrorist attacks.” He said the federal government had exhausted all avenues to bring together stakeholders and urge them to condemn terrorism by naming those involved, whether the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), or groups funded by India or Afghanistan. The state minister claimed that in 2013, when the government decided to hold talks with the TTP and representatives were proposed by both sides, the TTP had nominated PTI founder Imran Khan to its committee. He also alleged that the PTI founder had allowed the TTP to open offices in Peshawar. During his address, Chaudhry also criticised the PTI, showing a press release issued by the TTP that condemned the dismissal of the party’s government. Meanwhile, speaking at a press conference in Sialkot, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif criticised the JUI-F chief for constantly “targeting” the country’s security forces. He declared that the sacrifices made by the security forces, officers, and the public in the fight against terrorism were “matchless”. The defence minister referred to Fazl’s accusations that the emergency and governor’s rule were imposed to capture KP’s mineral resources, saying that he had shared a full list of people who had the mining contracts in KP. Asif maintained that the whole PTI and opposition leadership was engaged by the government before the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule. “But it was fruitless,” he said. “The situation will improve in KP […] parliament can roll back the decision of imposing the emergency only if the improvement of the situation in the province is guaranteed,” the defence minister said. He said that some individuals in KP were expecting to get a share in the administrative changes in the province. “We will ensure free and fair elections. Whenever the time comes, everybody can take part in it,” he said. Fazl’s remarks also prompted a response from KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, who has now been tasked with running the province under governor’s rule. Kundi, referring to the JUI-F chief, asked whether “your land in the land belonging to martyrs in DI Khan is halal”. “What you get is halal, what the other gets is haram,” he remarked. The governor reaffirmed that the new KP administration would continue to function properly. ‘Extremely upset’ Fazl, who was involved in reducing tensions between the Centre and the KP government, has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. He also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the two parties. Addressing a rally in Multan on Thursday, Fazl further recalled that his party had expressed reservations over the merger of tribal areas into KP after the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018. “We were not against the merger, but we said that it was an issue of the political future of the people of tribal areas,” he said, alleging that the people of those areas were not consulted on the merger. He alleged governor’s rule was not imposed in Balochistan because the province’s chief minister “praises you”. The next day, during an interaction with journalists, the interior minister said, “The head of a party is extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship.” This politician, Naqvi alleged, had remained “dependent on the establishment for decades to advance his political career”. “These are the same politicians who remained in politics for decades with the support of the establishment, and this politician even relied on the establishment to arrange air tickets for the members of his party,” he further alleged. He said such politicians had little justification for criticising others now, particularly after having benefitted from the same system they currently denounced. The same day, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also railed against Fazl in a post on X. She said it was not expected of a senior politician such as him to support those who facilitate terrorism — an apparent reference to the PTI, which the Centre accuses of backing terrorism. She also criticised Fazl for his remarks about Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, seemingly referring to his comments during the Multan address about the centralisation of power. The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Fazl, as well as Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan. In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release. Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI. Both sides had held separate meetings with Fazl, reportedly for his intervention to help break the deadlock in the negotiations.

items.title: 17 dead, 25 hurt in stampede at Durga Puja gathering in Kolkata
items.description: At least 17 people were killed and two dozen more injured on Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that was likely caused by sudden rainfall during a Hindu religious gathering, officials said. West Bengal’s Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 others were injured outside a pavilion “in a stampede” at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata. “Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said. A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining at night and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede”. Deadly crowd incidents are a frequent occurrence at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, due to poor management and safety lapses. In August, a stampede at a Hindu temple in Bihar killed at least seven people and injured 19 others. Last year, a stampede at India’s Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team’s first Indian Premier League title. The same year, 36 people were killed after a stampede broke out at a campaign rally of a popular actor-turned-politician in southern Tamil Nadu state. In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering.

items.title: Tunis | Une nouvelle peine de prison confirmée en appel contre Khayam Turki
items.description: L'activiste politique et homme d’affaires Khayam Turki, cumule désormais plusieurs condamnations assorties de lourdes peines de prison et d'importantes sanctions financières. La Cour d’appel de Tunis a ainsi confirmé une condamnation à quatre ans de prison ferme et à une amende de 200 000 dinars à l'encontre de Khayam Turki, et ce, dans le cadre d’affaires de fraude et de contentieux fiscaux, selon une source citée par Mosaïque FM, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026. Cette décision intervient parallèlement à un autre jugement prononcé par la Chambre criminelle spécialisée dans les affaires de corruption financière près le Tribunal de première instance de Tunis, qui l'a condamné à 14 ans de prison ferme, accompagnés d'une amende, pour des accusations de blanchiment d’argent, d'escroquerie et d'exploitation illégale de ses activités professionnelles et sociales. Ce verdict prévoit également une surveillance administrative pour une durée de cinq ans à l'issue de sa peine ainsi qu'une confiscation de l'ensemble de ses avoirs déposés auprès des établissements financiers tunisiens. Y. N. L’article Tunis | Une nouvelle peine de prison confirmée en appel contre Khayam Turki est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Unstoppable Barca thrash Betis to extend perfect start
items.description: Hansi Flick’s dominant Barcelona routed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday to return five points clear at the top of La Liga. Teenage winger Lamine Yamal scored a brilliant goal for the Spanish champions, with Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo also finding the net at La Cartuja stadium in Seville. Betis, third, had Facundo Bernal sent off for a headbutt on Yamal early in the second half of a pulsating clash. Barca set a new club record for victories at the start of a league campaign and equalled the all-time record of nine, set by Real Madrid in the 1968/69 season. Flick’s side boast 11 wins from 11 games across all competitions. “Once again the team has shown its attacking potential, but it’s also true we’re giving quite a bit away, and that’s probably where the improvement has to come from too,” Rodri told DAZN. Earlier Atletico, second, snatched a late 1-0 win at Espanyol and are five points behind Barca, while Betis are eight points adrift of the leaders and Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla on Sunday. Betis rested several players, including key midfielder Isco, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Feyenoord. Manuel Pellegrini’s side still gave Barca a stern test, after the Catalan giants went ahead through a sensational Yamal strike in the 10th minute. The 19-year-old turned sharply on the edge of the box to escape Bernal and then exquisitely curled into the top corner. “(It was) an incredible goal, we’ve got used to him doing this lately, I have to say,” added Rodri. “In the end, players like that make the difference. But I try to focus on the other things he brings… (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space.” – Defensive flaws – Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca’s clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark. A corner came all the way through the box and was recycled by Pablo Fornals, who crossed for Valentin Gomez to head home, getting in front of Barca defender Xavi Espart. Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts. However the Argentine midfielder’s long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis’ chagrin. Jesus extended Barca’s lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal’s cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside. Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides. Barca added their fourth when Pau Cubarsi nodded the ball across to Garcia to pounce from close range. It was the eighth time this season Flick’s free-scoring side have scored four goals or more in a match. The coach brought Raphinha on as a substitute after the Brazilian missed the previous two matches with an injury problem, taking off Yamal to prevent a potential further card and suspension for the Clasico next weekend. First comes the matter of a visit to the French capital on Tuesday to face reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain, which promises to be a thrilling match. Substitute Olmo finished the match off with a neat finish from the edge of the box as Betis backed off to allow Barca’s attention to turn to Europe. Betis defender Hector Bellerin said there were a “couple of unfair decisions” that went against his side but he was pleased with the team’s efforts against his former club. “Facing a team like this, with this quality, we stood up to them until the final minutes,” Bellerin told DAZN. “We showed that with 11 players we’re able to compete against the best.” The post Unstoppable Barca thrash Betis to extend perfect start appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Youth population is Nigeria’s greatest asset – Tinubu
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, OSOGBO President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that Nigeria’s greatest asset is not the mineral deposit beneath its soil but the creative youth population with there resilience and abundant talent. Read Also: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal Tinubu said this at the flag off construction of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Centre for Youth Empowerment and Inter-Cultural Dialogue at the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife Osun State at the weekend. The President was represented by the Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hazmat, said the event transcend a mere celebration but a national statement and deliberate investment in the aspiration of Nigeria’s young population. While describing that the establishment of the centre as timely and strategic, he said the centre offer opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship. His words, “Today is more than a ceremonial occasion. It is a statement of national purpose. It represents an investment in the aspirations of our young people, a commitment to the unity of our country, and a recognition that Nigeria’s greatest resource is not merely what lies beneath its soil, but the talent, creativity, resilience and enterprise of its people.” “The establishment of this Centre is therefore timely and strategic. It offers an opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship, engage with industry and international partners, and contribute to national development. He emphasised that the centre’s success should be measured by the opportunities it creates for young people and the lives it transforms. “The true value of this Centre will ultimately be determined not by the magnificence of its buildings, but by the quality of the opportunities it creates and the lives it transforms,” he stated. He also called for partnerships among universities, industries, government, investors and international development institutions to connect young people with economic opportunities and help transform their ideas into viable enterprises. He also highlighted the importance of mutual respect and understanding among people from different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds, with the aim of promoting national unity, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion. “Our expectation should be that, in the years ahead, this institution will be known not merely as a centre of learning, but as a centre of transformation—one that produces capable leaders, responsible citizens, innovative entrepreneurs and globally competitive professionals. “The Centre should provide a meeting point for universities, industry, government, investors, civil society and international development institutions,” the President said. In his welcome address, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simeon Bamire said the centre was conceived as a response to challenges confronting young people, including unemployment, limited access to skills development, unequal economic opportunities and social exclusion. He said the initiative would provide a sustainable platform for equipping young people with practical competencies, promoting enterprise and innovation, and connecting talent with meaningful opportunities. According to him, the centre would serve as an internationally recognised platform where young people from Nigeria, Africa and other parts of the world could learn, collaborate, innovate and develop solutions to shared challenges. “Its programmes would promote entrepreneurship, digital technology, leadership, creative enterprise and peacebuilding, while encouraging cooperation across cultural and national boundaries”, he added. The proposed centre will feature an international conference and dialogue complex, a digital innovation and learning duplex, an entrepreneurship and incubation hub, a scholars and creators lodge, a culture exhibition and community engagement centre, as well as administrative, research and support infrastructure. The project is expected to promote human capital development, employment and enterprise growth, peace, inclusion and social cohesion. It is also intended to provide networking opportunities and support research and policy development. The project is expected to provide young people with opportunities to learn, collaborate, innovate and engage across cultural boundaries. January was mentioned as a target for commissioning the building, although the year was not specified in the information obtained. Vanguard News The post Youth population is Nigeria’s greatest asset – Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .
