items.title: 2027: Northern govs pledge total support for Tinubu
items.description: …As Shekarau promises to hit ground running By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja ABUJA: Governors of the northern states have pledged 100 per cent support for President Bola Tinubu, insisting that the North must respect the 1999 understanding between the region and the South on power sharing. Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, spoke on behalf of all the Northern State Governors at the commissioning of the Arewa for Asiwaju A4A national secretariat in Abuja, performed by Vice President Kashim Shettima. “Everywhere, we support the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 100 per cent,” he said. Recalling the agreement, Sani said: “In 1999, there was a mutual agreement between the North and the South that the North would be allowed to go for two consecutive terms in office, and based on that, in the last dispensation, President Buhari, of blessed memory, served for two consecutive terms, meaning for eight years.” He said the South had “every opportunity to present a candidate or candidates,” but did not, because of that agreement and “especially with the support of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu.” Yusuf admitted the arrangement has no constitutional backing, but said that should not matter. “We don’t have any cause to now renege on that promise, even though it is not constitutional. But I can say the constitution of common sense. Common sense dictates that we have to respect this mutual agreement,” he said. The governor told the President that the northern states, “all democrats” and “all patriotic Northern states” were behind him. “He has done exceedingly well, as enumerated by our national chairman,” Sani said. He urged supporters to declare their position publicly. “Don’t be afraid, afraid of facts. We have all agreed we are members of the APC, and therefore, we must work together to ensure that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his Vice President emerge victorious come January 16, by the grace of Allah,” he said. Sani also asked the gathering to extend the same support “to all members of the National Assembly, as well as all governors in Nigeria and members of the State Assemblies.” The Chairman of the A4A Board of Trustees (BoT), Ibrahim Shekarau, thanked the Vice President for accepting to commission the building, describing him as “our leader in the northern part of Nigeria, the highest elected son of the land.” He also thanked the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying that “whatever anybody would do to promote the success of the APC, the main driver of the game is the leadership of the APC itself.” Shekarau acknowledged the National Assembly members led by the Deputy Senate President, the governors, former governors and the former National Assembly leadership. He also thanked coordinators and delegates from “all the 19 northern states, and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).” He told the secretariat’s directors and staff that the trustees would continue to back them “so that the inner room of the city will continue to fill us with marvellous programmes to achieve our goal.” “We have ten times more party supporters outside this building. We are determined. We are committed, and we will now hit the ground in our mission,” he said. The post 2027: Northern govs pledge total support for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Naturalisation en France depuis 2000 : les Marocains devancent les Algériens
items.description: Trois millions de personnes “ nées étrangères ” ont acquis la nationalité française depuis 2000, fait ressortir une étude menée sur la base des chiffres de l’Institut national des statistiques et des études économiques (INSEE). L'étude est réalisée par deux think-tank, la Fondation pour l’innovation politique (Fondapol) et l’Observatoire de l’immigration et de la démocratie (OID). Sur les 3 millions de nouveaux français, plus de la moitié, soit 1,6 million, ont obtenu la citoyenneté via une naturalisation par décret, 770 000 via le “ droit du sol différé ” et 560 000 à la suite du mariage avec une personne de nationalité française. Les auteurs de l'étude évoquent des chiffres “ sans précédent ”, soulignant qu’il y a eu près de deux fois plus d’acquisitions de la nationalité française sur le premier quart du 21e siècle que durant le dernier quart du siècle précédent. 323 000 Algériens ont acquis la nationalité française depuis 2004 Par provenance des naturalisés entre 2004 et 2023, soit en 20 ans, l'étude indique que plus d’un tiers d'entre eux (36 %) sont originaires du Maghreb. Avec 404 286 naturalisations, les Marocains arrivent en tête et sont “ la nationalité la plus nombreuse et constituent un sixième de l’ensemble des nouveaux Français par acquisition ”. Les Algériens sont en deuxième position avec 323 151, suivis des Tunisiens (146 043). Le top 5 est complété par les Turcs et les Portugais. L'étude relève que 83 % des Algériens ayant acquis une citoyenneté de l’Union européenne pendant la même période l’ont fait en devenant français, contre 61 % pour les Tunisiens et 28 % pour les Marocains. Les maghrébins et les Africains en force Si les Maghrébins constituent le tiers des nouveaux français, les personnes originaires de toute l’Afrique en constituent, elles, plus de 61 %. “ Près de deux tiers (61,5 %) des personnes ayant acquis la nationalité française entre 2004 et 2023 sont originaires du continent africain dans son ensemble – dont le Maghreb. Elles sont trois fois plus nombreuses que celles originaires d’Europe (20 %) ”, lit-on dans l'étude. Outre l’Algérie, le Maroc et la Tunisie, les “ Africains ” naturalisés français ces 20 dernières années viennent de toutes les régions du continent, principalement de la Côte d’Ivoire, du Mali, du Sénégal, du Congo-Brazzaville, du Cameroun, des Comores, de la République démocratique du Congo, et de la Guinée et Madagascar. Trois millions de visas et 377 000 titres de séjour en 2025 L'étude note par ailleurs qu'en plus des naturalisations, la France enregistre aussi un flux d’étrangers “ qui ne cesse de croître ”. Un total de 377 000 titres de séjour a été délivré en 2025, soit 32 000 primo-délivrances de plus en un an (+ 9,2 %). Il est aussi fait état d’une hausse de 6,4 % des renouvellements, en particulier pour motif familial (+ 10,5 %). Au 31 décembre 2025, 4,5 millions d'étrangers étaient présents sur le territoire français en situation régulière. Pendant la même année, la France a délivré 3 millions de visas. Malgré les 3 millions de naturalisations, le pourcentage des étrangers dans la population de la France a presque doublé, passant de 5,5 % en 1999 à 9,1 % en 2025, soit “ un record historique ”, lit-on. À noter que l'étude est très orientée, tendant à démontrer que ces chiffres sont électoralement favorables à La France Insoumise (LFI), étant donné que les nouveaux naturalisés, notamment ceux originaire du Maghreb et d'Afrique, sont supposés être plus enclins à voter pour le parti de Jean-Luc Mélenchon. items.title: Niger, gardons le calme et la confiance…
items.description: Les pénuries d’essence et de gasoil actuellement constatées à Niamey et dans d’autres villes du Niger suscitent des préoccupations légitimes au sein de la population. Ces difficultés perturbent les déplacements, les activités économiques, le transport des marchandises et le quotidien de nombreux citoyens. Face à cette situation, il est essentiel de garder son sang-froid, de faire preuve de patience et d’éviter toute panique inutile. Ces pénuries ne sont pas nécessairement durables. Leur résorption dépendra notamment du rétablissement des approvisionnements et de l’efficacité des mesures engagées par les autorités. Selon les données communiquées par le Gouvernement en octobre 2026, le déficit d’essence Super a atteint 196,62 millions de litres au cours des huit premiers mois de l’année, tandis que celui du gasoil s’élevait à 52,60 millions de litres. Ces chiffres montrent l’ampleur du défi à relever. Pour y répondre, les autorités ont annoncé des mesures visant à sécuriser l’approvisionnement, à renforcer la production de la Société de raffinage de Zinder (SORAZ) et à corriger les dysfonctionnements de la chaîne pétrolière. Ces initiatives sont importantes, même si leur efficacité dépendra de leur mise en œuvre et des résultats obtenus sur le terrain. Nous pouvons espérer une amélioration progressive de la situation, sans avancer de date précise pour un retour à la normale. Souvenons-nous que notre pays a déjà traversé des épreuves difficiles, notamment l’embargo de 2023 et les restrictions qui ont affecté notre économie en 2024. Malgré les contraintes, les Nigériens ont fait preuve de courage, d’adaptation et de solidarité. Cette expérience nous rappelle que notre capacité collective à surmonter les difficultés constitue une force précieuse. Aujourd’hui encore, nous devons faire preuve de cette même résilience. Évitons les achats excessifs, les spéculations et la propagation de rumeurs susceptibles d’aggraver la situation. Restons attentifs aux informations officielles et soutenons-nous mutuellement, particulièrement les personnes dont les activités et les revenus sont directement affectés par ces pénuries. Le Niger nous appartient à tous. Au-delà des difficultés du moment, nous partageons une même patrie et un avenir commun à construire. Aimons notre pays, préservons notre unité et contribuons chacun, à notre niveau, à sa stabilité et à son développement. Dans cet esprit, les citoyens qui le souhaitent peuvent continuer à soutenir les orientations des autorités de la Refondation, sous la conduite de Son Excellence le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, Chef de l’État et Président de la République, ainsi que du Conseil national pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP). Il est également essentiel que les mesures annoncées produisent des résultats concrets pour améliorer durablement l’approvisionnement en carburant et soulager les populations. Les difficultés actuelles ne doivent pas nous faire perdre confiance en notre capacité collective à avancer. Le Niger dispose de ressources naturelles, de compétences humaines et d’atouts économiques importants. Leur valorisation, associée au travail, à la solidarité et à une gestion efficace des ressources, peut contribuer à améliorer les conditions de vie de nos concitoyens. Gardons notre calme, restons unis et faisons preuve de résilience. Les pénuries actuelles constituent une difficulté à traiter avec sérieux et responsabilité, mais elles ne doivent pas nous faire oublier notre capacité à surmonter les épreuves. Aimons le Niger et continuons à travailler pour un pays plus fort, plus autonome et plus prospère. Les jours meilleurs se construisent par la patience, le travail, la solidarité et l’engagement de tous. Par Ousmane Jazy L’article Niger, gardons le calme et la confiance… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: Le gouvernement prend les devants
items.description: À l’issue de l’atelier sur la Tabaski, le ministre en charge de l’Élevage, Me Ousmane Diagne, a tiré un bilan globalement satisfaisant de la campagne 2026. Pour celle de 2027, prévue à la mi-mai, il compte sur la capitalisation des bonnes leçons, voire sur leur amélioration, avec pour ambition de financer la production. RUFISQUE – « Gouverner, c’est prévoir », a-t-on l’habitude de dire. À sept mois de l’édition 2027 de la Tabaski, le ministre en charge de l’Élevage, Me Ousmane Diagne, a pris les devants en organisant un atelier dédié. Cette rencontre a réuni une panoplie d’acteurs du sous-secteur de l’élevage ainsi que des partenaires (Forces de défense et de sécurité, banques, etc.), le jeudi 15 octobre 2026. « D’habitude, l’atelier d’évaluation se déroulait au mois de mars. L’organiser dès le mois d’octobre nous laisse une marge de manœuvre assez importante pour essayer d’améliorer ce qui a été fait de bon, mais surtout de rectifier ce qui doit l’être », a-t-il déclaré. Les acteurs, surtout les éleveurs, ont unanimement salué la démarche anticipative de la tutelle, qui consiste à prendre à bras-le-corps l’opération Tabaski. Les échanges portant sur cette question et sur les sujets connexes ont duré plus de six tours d’horloge. Faisant un feedback sur la campagne 2026, le ministre en tire un bilan satisfaisant. « Globalement, le bilan a été une réussite. Sur un objectif de 900.000 moutons, nous en avons obtenu 1.069.356 têtes, soit 118,82 %, avec un reliquat de 144.727 sujets enregistrés au lendemain de la fête », souligne-t-il. Selon lui, ces résultats probants ont été obtenus grâce à l’accompagnement de l’État, à travers le Fonds d’appui à la stabulation (Fonstab), et au soutien des partenaires financiers. Un bilan relativisé par les éleveurs qui mettent en avant le nombre important d’invendus, pointant du doigt l’ouverture du marché aux importations. Sur ce point, ils se sont toutefois montrés cléments et indulgents envers Me Diagne qui n’était pas en poste lors de la précédente campagne. En vue de la réussite de la campagne 2027 déjà engagée, les éleveurs ont saisi l’occasion pour exposer à l’autorité leurs doléances, portant singulièrement sur l’urgence de mettre en place une gouvernance adaptée (organisation des points de vente, cherté de l’aliment pour le bétail, lutte contre le vol de bétail, abattages clandestins, financement, etc.), afin de garantir le bon déroulement de l’opération Tabaski. Attentif à leurs requêtes, le ministre promet, avec l’appui de ses services, notamment du département de l’Élevage, d’y apporter des solutions. Au-delà du maintien des acquis tirés de la précédente édition, l’ambition de la tutelle est désormais de financer la production. Ainsi, Ousmane Diagne affirme que les prochains financements viseront particulièrement les acteurs de la production. La finalité est de faire en sorte que ce que la population consomme pour la Tabaski soit produit au Sénégal. Mohamed DIÈNE (Correspondant)

items.title: La Tunisie, invitée d’honneur de MTL CONNECTE 2027
items.description: Dans le cadre des efforts visant à renforcer la coopération tuniso-canadienne dans les domaines de la technologie, de l'innovation et de la transformation numérique, M. Kamel Makkes, Consul de la République Tunisienne à Montréal, a pris part, au nom de l'Ambassadeur de Tunisie au Canada, à la 8ème édition du Forum MTL CONNECTE 2026, qui s'est tenue à Montréal du 13 au 16 octobre 2026. Il a également présidé les travaux de la rencontre des compétences tunisiennes « Tunisia Global Forum », organisée à la succursale Desjardins-Montréal, à l'initiative du Réseau Tuniso-Canadien des Affaires (RTCA). Cet événement a favorisé le réseautage entre des entrepreneurs, experts et investisseurs tunisiens et canadiens et permis d'explorer de nouvelles pistes de partenariat dans des secteurs porteurs, tels que les technologies de l'information, l'intelligence artificielle et la recherche scientifique. Lors de cette manifestation, le flambeau a été officiellement transmis à la Tunisie, désignée invitée d'honneur de l'édition 2027 de MTL CONNECTE, en signe de reconnaissance de son potentiel technologique, de la qualité de ses ressources humaines et de son rôle au sein de l'écosystème mondial de l'innovation. L'Ambassade, en collaboration avec le Réseau Tuniso-Canadien des Affaires (RTCA) et les institutions économiques de soutien, ambitionne de faire de l'édition 2027 une plateforme pour le développement de la coopération, la concrétisation de projets et l'établissement de partenariats durables entre les institutions économiques, universitaires et les centres de recherche en Tunisie et au Canada, au service de l'intérêt commun. items.title: Diaz dazzles as Bayern batter Leipzig to go top
items.description: Luis Diaz hit a hat-trick as Bayern Munich pummelled a listless RB Leipzig 6-1 at home on Saturday to climb to the top of the Bundesliga table. Borussia Dortmund had edged ahead of Freiburg into top spot after their earlier draw at Union Berlin, but Bayern responded in typically ruthless fashion to take the summit. The dominant display was Bayern’s best performance of the season and will boost their confidence days out from Wednesday’s home Champions League clash with English champions Arsenal. Diaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life to terrorise Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left. In his 100th Bundesliga match, Harry Kane scored a goal and laid on two assists as he pulled the strings from deep while Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet. Confined to his chair with a hip complaint, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany produced a masterclass against opposite number Martin Demichelis, his former Manchester City teammate. Bayern have now won their past three games against Leipzig by a combined scoreline of 17-1. Bayern had drawn their past two matches, a rare run of middling form for the German giants, but shook off the funk early, with Diaz, Pavlovic and Olise putting the hosts in control before half-time. Diaz scored either side of a Kane tap-in after the break, with the England captain withdrawn before the hour mark ahead of old rivals Arsenal’s visit. Leipzig’s Andrija Maksimovic got on the board with a late late consolation in stoppage time. Dortmund draw in Berlin Dortmund missed a chance to stay ahead of Bayern after being held to a scoreless draw at Union Berlin. After starting the season strongly with six wins in a row in all competitions, Dortmund have stalled of late, drawing two and losing one of their last three matches. “We simply have to get better in attack. Right now, it’s just not good enough,” Dortmund’s Waldemar Anton told Sky. Serhou Guirassy had a golden chance to snatch all three points for his side at the end of a match of few opportunities, but headed just wide with 11 minutes remaining to cap a poor game up front for the Dortmund striker. It was the first draw between the two sides in their history, with each of their previous 16 clashes in all competitions producing a winner. Compounding Dortmund’s woes was a serious-looking ankle injury to substitute midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas, who was helped from the pitch just eight minutes after coming on. “Let’s hope it’s not too serious. He’s not feeling great right now,” Dortmund sporting director Ole Book told reporters. Stuttgart suffered a blow ahead of Tuesday’s home Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, going down 1-0 at Hamburg after an 88th-minute Miro Muheim goal. Stuttgart are languishing in 13th in the Bundesliga with two wins and four defeats but have impressed in Europe this season to sit in fourth spot in the 36-team Champions League table after two matches. Elsewhere, promoted Elversberg continued their impressive debut season in the top flight, winning 4-3 at home to Augsburg. Lukas Petkov, Lasse Guenther, Maximilian Rohr and Frederik Schmahl got on the scoresheet as Elversberg, from the smallest town to ever host a Bundesliga side, climbed to sixth in the table. Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the fifth straight Bundesliga match as his brace helped Werder Bremen come from two goals down to draw 2-2 at home against Paderborn. The Germany striker returned to Bremen on loan after an unhappy spell at West Ham but now has seven goals in seven games in all competitions. A first-half goal for Phillip Tietz was enough for Mainz to win 1-0 at Schalke and climb to fifth in the standings. items.title: Macky Sall, le rêve brisé
items.description: Le 17 octobre 2026, Macky Sall a officiellement retiré sa candidature au poste de Secrétaire général des Nations unies. L’ancien président sénégalais espérait succéder à António Guterres, dont le mandat prend fin le 31 décembre 2026. Malgré le soutien du président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye et du président burundais Évariste Ndayishimiye, son ambition s’est heurtée à la réalité des rapports de force internationaux. Le vote informel du Conseil de sécurité, organisé le 16 octobre, a été particulièrement défavorable. Selon les informations rapportées, Macky Sall a obtenu 5 avis favorables contre 10 défavorables. Ce résultat a révélé les limites de sa candidature auprès des membres de l’instance chargée de recommander le futur Secrétaire général. Pour accéder à ce poste, le soutien de quelques chefs d’État ne suffit pas. Il faut obtenir une recommandation du Conseil de sécurité, où les États-Unis, la Chine, la Russie, la France et le Royaume-Uni disposent chacun d’un droit de veto. Un seul de ces cinq pays peut donc bloquer une candidature, même soutenue par plusieurs États. Macky Sall a-t-il cru qu’un rapprochement avec Emmanuel Macron pouvait faciliter son accession au sommet des Nations unies ? La question mérite d’être posée au regard de l’évolution des rapports entre la France et l’Afrique. Depuis plusieurs années, l’influence française recule dans une partie du continent, particulièrement au Sahel. En 2025, la France a achevé la restitution de ses dernières installations militaires au Sénégal, dans le cadre de la redéfinition de la coopération entre les deux pays. En mai 2026, Emmanuel Macron a participé au sommet Africa Forward au Kenya, dans un contexte où Paris cherche à renouveler ses relations avec les États africains. Ces événements traduisent une réalité que les dirigeants africains ne peuvent ignorer. La France reste une puissance importante, mais elle ne décide pas seule de l’avenir politique et géopolitique du continent. Les intérêts américains, chinois, russes et britanniques pèsent également sur les grandes décisions internationales. Penser que la proximité avec le président français suffit à ouvrir les portes des institutions mondiales, c’est sous-estimer la complexité des rapports de force. L’expérience récente invite donc les dirigeants africains à la prudence. Les alliances avec Paris peuvent servir certains intérêts, mais elles ne constituent jamais une garantie de réussite. Les intérêts français et les priorités africaines ne coïncident pas systématiquement. Le soutien de Bassirou Diomaye Faye à son prédécesseur constitue un autre élément marquant. Élu en mars 2024 après une campagne portée par la volonté de rupture avec l’ancien pouvoir, le président sénégalais a finalement soutenu la candidature internationale de Macky Sall. Ce choix pouvait être présenté comme une démarche en faveur du rayonnement du Sénégal. Pourtant, le résultat du vote a montré les limites de cette mobilisation. Malgré les appuis de Dakar et de Bujumbura, Macky Sall n’a pas obtenu les soutiens nécessaires pour poursuivre sa candidature dans des conditions favorables. Cette situation rappelle une vérité diplomatique. La solidarité entre dirigeants africains peut renforcer une candidature, mais elle ne remplace ni les négociations internationales ni les accords avec les puissances qui disposent du pouvoir de décision. L’ambition internationale de Macky Sall se heurtait également aux controverses laissées par ses douze années au pouvoir, de 2012 à 2024. Les dernières années de sa présidence ont été marquées par de fortes tensions politiques, des arrestations d’opposants et des violences lors de manifestations. En février 2024, sa décision de reporter l’élection présidentielle a provoqué une grave crise institutionnelle. Le Conseil constitutionnel a invalidé ce report, et l’élection s’est finalement tenue en mars 2024. Ces événements ont durablement marqué la vie politique sénégalaise et alimenté les critiques des organisations de défense des droits humains. Un ancien président qui aspire à diriger les Nations unies doit s’attendre à ce que son bilan soit examiné. La fonction de Secrétaire général exige une capacité à dialoguer avec des gouvernements aux intérêts opposés, mais aussi une crédibilité sur les questions de paix, de démocratie et de droits humains. Il serait toutefois excessif d’affirmer que ces controverses expliquent, à elles seules, les résultats du vote. Les motivations précises des membres du Conseil de sécurité ne sont pas toutes connues. Le retrait de Macky Sall constitue un revers pour sa candidature, mais il ne doit pas être confondu avec une défaite de l’Afrique entière. Le continent compte 54 États membres de l’ONU et près de 1,5 milliard d’habitants, mais ne dispose toujours pas de siège permanent au Conseil de sécurité. Cette situation justifie une réforme de la gouvernance mondiale et une représentation africaine plus équitable. Pour atteindre cet objectif, les pays africains doivent mieux coordonner leurs positions, préparer leurs candidatures et construire des alliances qui dépassent les intérêts personnels ou les proximités politiques. Le 17 octobre 2026, Macky Sall a justifié son retrait par les résultats du processus de sélection et par la préférence qu’il estimait percevoir en faveur d’une candidature d’Amérique latine et des Caraïbes, éventuellement portée par une femme. Son parcours rappelle que le soutien d’un président, même influent, ne suffit pas à faire aboutir une ambition internationale. Les relations diplomatiques reposent sur des intérêts qui évoluent, des compromis parfois difficiles et des rapports de force qu’aucun dirigeant ne maîtrise seul. Les dirigeants africains doivent cesser de croire que les conseils d’Emmanuel Macron constituent une garantie de succès politique ou géopolitique. L’avenir du continent ne peut dépendre des orientations d’une puissance étrangère, quelle qu’elle soit. L’Afrique a besoin de partenariats diversifiés, mais aussi de dirigeants capables d’analyser les intérêts de leurs interlocuteurs, de défendre leur souveraineté et de prendre leurs décisions en toute indépendance. Le rêve de Macky Sall s’est arrêté devant la réalité diplomatique. La leçon est simple. Un partenariat peut être utile, mais une dépendance politique peut coûter cher. La véritable force d’un dirigeant réside dans sa capacité à défendre les intérêts de son pays sans confier son avenir aux calculs d’une autre capitale. Par Ousmane Jazy Souleymane L’article Macky Sall, le rêve brisé est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: 17 dead, 25 injured in stampede at religious gathering
items.description: At least 17 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that was likely caused by sudden rainfall during a Hindu religious gathering, officials said. West Bengal’s Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 others were injured outside a pavilion “in a stampede” at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata. “Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said. A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining at night and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.” Deadly crowd incidents are a frequent occurrence at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, due to poor management and safety lapses. Last year, a stampede at India’s Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team’s first Indian Premier League title. The same year, 36 people were killed after a stampede broke out at a campaign rally of a popular actor-turned-politician in southern Tamil Nadu state. In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering. items.title: Zambia launches oral cholera vaccination campaign to contain outbreak
items.description: Zambia on Friday launched an oral cholera vaccination campaign targeting Lusaka, the capital and epicenter of the current outbreak, alongside Chibombo District in the country's Central Province. More than 500,000 vaccine doses are expected to be allocated to the two districts in the first phase of the campaign, while an additional 480,000 doses are expected to arrive soon for distribution to other affected areas. Speaking at the launch, Health Minister Roma Chilengi said the targeted campaign aims to protect people in the hardest-hit areas while ensuring the efficient use of limited global vaccine supplies. He reaffirmed the government's commitment to eliminating cholera as a public health threat and expressed gratitude to cooperating partners and the private sector for supporting the delivery of essential medical services to affected communities. Chilengi said the outbreak had spread to 12 districts across five provinces. Zambia has recorded 966 cumulative cholera cases, including 43 new cases in the past 24 hours, and 25 deaths, the minister added.

items.title: ‘I can’t die like this’: flydubai pilot recounts ordeal of cockpit attack
items.description: The captain of a flydubai flight whose co-pilot attacked him with an axe in an alleged bid to bring down the plane said one thought kept running through his head as the harrowing ordeal unfolded: “You can’t die like this.” Read Also: ‘I could not let all those people die’ — Indian pilot recounts flydubai ordeal Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recounted the “traumatic” experience to Sky News Arabia in his first interview since the incident late last month in which he, passengers and other crew members were credited with averting disaster on the Tel Aviv-bound flight. With his head and one hand bandaged and glasses perched on his nose, Machchhar spoke from his hospital bed in the UAE. “My vision was restricted to a few inches,” said the pilot, describing the effect of being struck in the back of the head with an emergency axe by his co-pilot, who had positioned himself behind Machchhar’s seat. At first thinking that a part of the airplane’s ceiling had come loose, he then received several more blows and was wounded in the hand as he tried to shield himself. Machchhar recalled struggling to open the cockpit door so another pilot who was travelling on board could get inside. “So I was screaming his name and I was trying, because the switch that was very close to me to open the door, I was trying to just get help in,” he said. “But I remember being able to open the door,” he went on, only for it to shut again. “And at that point, I felt all the blood, you know, everything rushing down, my energy, everything, I was just, I was barely staying in consciousness.” “Soon after that, that was the time when I heard the engine sounds going down. And then immediately after that I felt the aircraft going into a dive.” According to findings released by the Emirati attorney general, Machchhar’s 29-year-old Omani co-pilot had planned to use the plane to carry out a suicide attack on the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, inspired by the September 11, 2001 attacks in New York. He claimed to have acted alone, something investigators are still working to verify. The prosecutor found that the other pilot on board, having seen the cockpit door open and close “in an unusual manner”, entered the flight deck and with the help of another crew member and passengers, subdued the co-pilot and regained control of the aircraft. The jet, which plunged violently during the fray, was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Machchhar said the way his colleague was able to intervene and safely land the plane was “commendable”. “It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die.” The post ‘I can’t die like this’: flydubai pilot recounts ordeal of cockpit attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gunmen kill two policemen, set station, operation van ablaze in Abia
items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe Unknown gunmen have killed two policemen and burnt buildings and a patrol van at the Uratta Police Division, in Aba, Abia State. Confirming the incident, Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the Command, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed that the hoodlums attacked the division with explosives, resulting in a fire that damaged part of the building and the divisional patrol van. She added that two police officers lost their lives, while three inspectors sustained injuries and are currently receiving medical attention. The Command further clarified that no firearms or ammunition were carted away by the attackers during the incident. The PPRO explained that the Commissioner of Police, Abia State Command, CP Wilfred Afolabi, had personally led an operational team to the area. She also stated that the team combed the surrounding environment and restored calm, while intensified security operations and monitoring are ongoing to apprehend the hoodlums. The PPRO assured that the Command will deploy all necessary operational and intelligence resources to identify and apprehend those responsible, assuring that the hoodlums will be brought to justice. “The Command extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of the fallen officers and the entire Police family over this painful loss. “Residents are urged to remain calm, vigilant and to support the Police with credible information that could assist the ongoing investigation. “Information can be reported at the nearest police station, through the suggestion boxes and contact details of the DPO’s provided at police divisions, or via the Command’s emergency hotlines: 08035415405,08079210004, 08079210005, 08079210006.” Vanguard gathered that Governor Alex Otti had visited the police station as well as the injured policemen at the hospital. items.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats, beat French mayor
items.description: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy of European diplomats and beat up a visiting French mayor, in a new escalation of violence during the Palestinian olive harvest, witnesses and diplomats told AFP. The 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France, kicked him and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank alongside the top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats. “I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, told AFP after he was attacked. “The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said. “For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.” Baudoux, who was wearing a sash with the French tricolour, was seen collapsed on the side of the car after the attack but he did not need hospital care. The attack came just one day after settlers beat an American photographer for The Washington Post, who was in moderate condition with broken vertebrae on Saturday. Israel’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation. But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, days away from an election in which he is seeking to shore up support from the far-right, instead alleged a “smear” campaign against settlers. Netanyahu said the diplomats should have coordinated their movements with the Israeli military and pointed out that Baudoux is a communist known for supporting the Palestinian cause. “We urge caution before drawing conclusions” about the attacks, Netanyahu’s office said in a statement. His main rival in October 27 elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, strongly criticised Netanyahu over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the State of Israel still possesses”. The attacks are “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”, Eisenkot said. Belgium called for an end to “impunity for violent settlers” after the latest attack. Attacks on cultural symbol Baudoux, the mayor, said he had come to the town of Taybeh, a Christian stronghold, along with his local pastor from France to sign a goodwill agreement. He was attacked just as he joined the harvest as a symbolic gesture with the Palestinians, for whom olives are an important cultural symbol. Extremist Israelis have issued calls to stop the Palestinians’ harvest after months of growing attacks in which settlers have stolen land and property. There has also been violence against Israelis, with a Palestinian shooting dead a settler last month. Bashar Fawadleh, a priest in Taybeh, said settlers had already attacked the harvest and snatched olives before beating the mayor. “One person was hit in the head and needed stitches. They also beat up an older lady in her 70s after insulting her with very bad words,” the pastor told AFP. The West Bank violence has shocked much of the world, with Britain leading economic sanctions that in turn caused Netanyahu to voice outrage. Netanyahu had also sought to throw doubt on the circumstances behind the beating Friday of the photographer, Heidi Levine, suggesting that Palestinians and “far-left” activists caused trouble. But President Isaac Herzog, who holds a mostly symbolic role, took the initiative Saturday to call Levine in the hospital, calling the attack “outrageous and shocking” and saying it weighed on his conscience. Israel Gantz, head of an umbrella settler group, blamed the recent incidents on “groups of provocateurs and terrorists” and implicitly acknowledged some Israelis’ responsibility, saying that they caused harm to the settlers’ cause. Settlers earlier this month also beat up AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh as he covered the olive harvest tensions, fracturing several of his ribs. Netanyahu’s government has ramped up approval of West Bank settlements, which are illegal under international law. Some 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank, which Israel seized in 1967, alongside three million Palestinians. items.title: EC must command public confidence regardless of which party is in power – Victoria Bright
items.description: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has called for consistency in the appointment of Electoral Commission (EC) officials, stressing that the Commission must command public confidence regardless of which political party is in power. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, she said the appointment of the two new Deputy Chairpersons of the EC must be assessed against consistent standards of constitutional legality, professional suitability and public confidence in their independence. “I think we must approach this issue with a consistent principle. And that principle is that the Electoral Commission must command public confidence, regardless of which party is in government,” she said. Ms Bright cautioned against changing the standards applied to appointments whenever political power changes hands, arguing that the credibility of the electoral body depends not only on the legality of its appointments but also on whether Ghanaians have confidence in its impartiality. She identified three key questions that should guide the assessment of the appointments: whether the constitutional requirements had been met, whether the appointees were suitable for their respective positions, and whether the process provided citizens with reasonable grounds to trust their independence. According to her, these questions are related but must be considered separately. She noted that the 1992 Constitution empowers the President to appoint Electoral Commissioners on the advice of the Council of State, while also protecting the Commission from external direction or control in the performance of its functions. Although she acknowledged that the appointments were not unconstitutional, she said concerns remained about their implications for public confidence in the institution. “The appointments are not unconstitutional, but they do cause concern,” she said. Ms Bright argued that, for an institution as sensitive as the EC, the perception of independence was almost as important as independence itself. She said the central issue was not simply whether the appointments were lawful, but whether they inspired confidence in the neutrality of the Commission across the political divide. Addressing the appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo, Ms Bright said concerns about her perceived political affiliations were relevant to the wider discussion about public confidence in the EC. She argued that her reported close association with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) provided a basis for citizens to question how the appointing authorities had considered the potential implications for perceptions of impartiality. However, Ms Bright stressed that Agbenyo’s qualifications and professional experience deserved fair consideration, adding that competence alone did not automatically resolve questions about independence. “For me, her qualifications and professional experience do deserve fair consideration. But both competence and independence are necessary for this kind of appointment. And evidence of one does not automatically answer questions about the other,” she said. On the appointment of Dr Joseph Kweku Asamoah, she acknowledged that his previous experience within the EC was relevant to his new role. NPP and NDC challenged to maintain consistency Ms Bright also recalled the controversy surrounding appointments to the EC under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, including the appointment of Chairperson Jean Mensa, who is allegedly related to the former First Lady, Rebecca Akufo-Addo. She said those appointments attracted objections from civil society organisations, including the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO), as well as criticism from the NDC, which was then in opposition. In her view, the history of those disagreements meant that both the NPP and the NDC had questions of consistency to answer over their positions on appointments to the electoral body. For the NPP, she said the question was why concerns about partisan associations should carry decisive weight under the current administration when similar concerns were resisted while the party was in government. For the NDC, she questioned how its own appointments measured up to the standards it had demanded when it was in opposition. Ms Bright maintained that political parties should uphold the principles they advocated while in opposition once they assumed office. She cautioned that controversial appointments made by previous administrations should not become a justification for repeating similar controversies. “Earlier controversial appointments cannot become a standing justification for further controversial appointments. We can’t keep going on and on,” she said. Bright questions argument about balancing EC composition The private legal practitioner also expressed concern about the reported explanation from the government side that the appointments were intended to rebalance the composition of the EC. She said such an argument would be troubling if the balance being discussed referred to partisan representation within the Commission. According to her, the EC should not be viewed as a body made up of representatives of competing political interests whose appointments are intended to counterbalance one another. Ms Bright warned that such an approach could undermine the Commission’s role as an impartial arbiter of the electoral process. She maintained that the priority should be to protect the independence and credibility of the institution rather than to create a perception that its composition reflects a political contest between the governing party and the opposition. Her comments come after President John Dramani Mahama swore in Dr Asamoah and Ms Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the EC on October 16.

items.title: Hydrocarbures : l’Algérie mobilise 71,6 milliards $ d’investissements à l’horizon 2030
items.description: L’Algérie a lancé des investissements massifs de 71,6 milliards de dollars pour augmenter sa production d’hydrocarbures à l’horizon 2030. Ce montant a été dévoilé par le ministre des Hydrocarbures, Mohamed Arkab, ce samedi 17 octobre, devant la Commission des finances et du budget de l’APN lors de la présentation du bilan de son secteur et du Projet de loi de finances 2027 . L’Algérie s’est fixée deux objectifs majeurs dans le domaine du pétrole et gaz . Le premier est d’augmenter la production primaire d'hydrocarbures à « environ 201 millions de tonnes équivalent pétrole (tep) d'ici 2030 », a précisé le ministre. La production algérienne d’hydrocarbures devrait atteindre 193 millions TEP en 2026, selon les prévisions de M. Arkab. Le second est « d’accroître le taux de transformation et de valorisation des hydrocarbures » en Algérie pour « dépasser 50 % de la production primaire, contre environ 30 % actuellement », a détaillé M. Arkab. Algérie : 13 milliards de dollars d’investissements dans la pétrochimie à l’horizon 2030 Pour atteindre ces deux objectifs, l’Algérie a réservé une « enveloppe d'investissement estimée à environ 71,6 milliards de dollars » pour le développement du secteur des hydrocarbures, dont « 52 milliards de dollars destinés aux activités en amont et environ 13 milliards de dollars aux projets de raffinage et de pétrochimie », a développé le ministre. Parmi les principaux projets pétrochimiques lancés par l’Algérie et qui sont en cours de réalisation figurent la raffinerie de Hassi Messaoud, une unité de production de Méthyl Tert-Butyl Ether (MTBE), un complexe de production de polypropylène à Arzew, un projet similaire en Turquie, ainsi qu'une unité de production d'Alkyl Benzène linéaire à Skikda. Le ministre a fait état de la hausse de la demande européenne en gaz algérien ainsi que le renouvellement et la signature de contrats d'approvisionnement à long terme avec plusieurs partenaires, dont l'Italie, l'Espagne, la Slovénie, la Tchéquie et l'Allemagne. L’article Hydrocarbures : l’Algérie mobilise 71,6 milliards $ d’investissements à l’horizon 2030 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: NDC must dissociate itself from Obuasi SHTS head over sexual abuse allegations – Vicky Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer Victoria Bright has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to dissociate itself from the head of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), who is reportedly seeking political office, amid sexual abuse allegations against him. She said anyone facing such serious allegations should not be given greater political influence while the matter remains under scrutiny, stressing the need to protect students and establish the facts through a fair investigation. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright questioned why the headmaster would seek political office amid the allegations. “This is exactly the problem with our country. Why should someone like that be contesting for a political post? It is something that defies all logic and all reasoning. I do not understand,” she said. Read also: Obuasi SHTS head accused of sexually abusing students is NDC Juaben secretary seeking chairmanship Ms Bright said the governing party should distance itself from the individual, saying that people facing serious allegations of abuse should not be placed in positions that could increase their power or influence. “And if I were part of the governing party, I would disassociate myself from someone like that. These are not the kind of people who should be given more power. They should not be empowered to carry on perpetrating these kinds of acts,” she said. Her comments come amid public concern over the sexual abuse allegations involving the head of Obuasi SHTS. Ms Bright said the response to the allegations should focus on protecting students, establishing the facts and holding anyone found responsible accountable. She said that the allegations must be investigated fairly, with the evidence guiding any decisions on responsibility. “The measure of our response will be whether students are protected, whether the allegations are fairly investigated, and whether responsibility is established wherever the evidence leads,” she said. Describing the allegations as a serious breach of trust, the lawyer called for a thorough investigation into the headmaster’s conduct. She also said the need to establish what other people who may have had knowledge of the alleged incidents did about them. “The key question for me is what each responsible person knew, when they knew it, and what they did next,” she said. Ms Bright called for the matter to be treated with the seriousness it deserved, given the potential risks to students and the responsibility of school authorities to protect them. She said the headmaster should face prosecution and imprisonment if an investigation established his guilt. “It’s a total abuse of trust, and he must be fully investigated and jailed if he’s found to be culpable,” she said. This comes after JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni said the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, who has been suspended over sexual abuse allegations against female students, is a serving constituency secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and an aspirant for the chairmanship position. According to him, the headmaster intends to contest the chairmanship at the party’s constituency delegates’ conference, expected before the end of the year.

items.title: Trump deals with Putin, so why should Ghana fear BRICS? – Ablakwa asks
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has defended Ghana’s pursuit of BRICS membership, arguing that the United States’ own dealings with Russia demonstrate the importance of pursuing national interests. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Mr Ablakwa cited President Donald Trump’s recent diesel agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to challenge warnings that Ghana’s engagement with the bloc could attract American sanctions. He argued that Ghana should not be discouraged from building relations with BRICS countries while Washington continued to pursue economic agreements with those same nations. Mr Ablakwa said that while critics were urging Ghana to fear Mr Trump’s influence, the US President was making strategic decisions to advance American interests. “If we really analyse this, President Trump has not stopped dealing with these BRICS countries. He (Donald Trump) has just got into a deal with Russia, President Putin, for diesel as his midterm elections approach, and President Zelensky (Ukrainian President) is furious,” “So we are being told that because of threats from President Trump, our foreign policies should be determined by threats that other countries may be putting out when those same countries are themselves being strategic, being smart, and they are dealing with the countries that you are afraid to deal with,” he argued. Read Also: Ghana risks 10% to 100% tariffs on exports to US under Trump’s threats as it moves to join BRICS He also pointed to economic ties between China and the United States as evidence that cooperation could continue despite political differences. “Indeed, China remains the biggest creditor to the US.” The Minister linked Ghana’s BRICS ambitions to the vision of the country’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, presenting the move as consistent with his pursuit of international solidarity and economic independence. His comments followed concerns, particularly from the opposition New Patriotic Party, about the possible implications of closer engagement with the bloc for Ghana’s relations with Washington. On October 6, Mr Ablakwa announced that Cabinet had approved Ghana’s decision to formally apply to join BRICS, saying the move would diversify international partnerships and create opportunities for trade, investment and economic cooperation. The Trump–Putin agreement cited by the Minister was announced on October 9 following a telephone conversation between the two leaders. According to Reuters, Mr Trump said Russia would supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets as part of efforts to reduce fuel prices. The arrangement involved easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports. It drew criticism from Ukraine and US lawmakers concerned that the additional revenue could support Moscow’s war effort.

items.title: Asking Agbenyo to resign will mean everyone else at EC must leave – Vicky Bright
items.description: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has described calls for newly appointed Electoral Commission (EC) Deputy Chairperson Emelia Affi Agbenyo to resign as excessive, arguing that applying the same standard to other commissioners could require the entire Commission to step down. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright said the focus should be on improving the appointment process to ensure that the EC commands public confidence, rather than singling out one appointee for resignation. Her comments follow a call by the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) for Ms Agbenyo to resign over concerns about her past political activities and their potential impact on public confidence in the Commission’s independence and impartiality. Ms Bright argued that demanding Ms Agbenyo’s resignation while allowing other commissioners with perceived political affiliations to remain in office would amount to applying different standards to individuals serving on the same institution. “I think that’s a step too far. If they are saying that, then everybody there should resign, from the EC Chair down. The EC Chair, we know, has a very strong family and political affiliation with the opposition party,” she said. She added that other members of the Commission also had political affiliations, questioning why one individual should be singled out for resignation while others remained in office. “So you can’t pick and choose. You can’t choose one and say resign, and this one stays and all of that. We are where we are,” she said. READ ALSO: CODEO calls for Emelia Agbnyo’s resignation over partisan ties Ms Bright said the focus should instead be on addressing the weaknesses in the process for appointing members of the EC to prevent similar controversies in the future. She maintained that previous administrations had made appointments that attracted criticism over perceived political affiliations, adding that the country needed to move beyond the recurring disagreements and consider the kind of electoral management body it wanted to establish. She argued that the debate should not be limited to whether appointments made by one administration were acceptable while those made by another were not. According to her, successive governments had appointed individuals perceived to be aligned with their respective political parties, making it necessary to reconsider the process rather than continue the cycle. “Every party that has come into power has appointed its own people. So for me, we should now look beyond that and ask ourselves a very, very important question. The test for me is what kind of Electoral Commission that we want to build,” she said. EC must inspire confidence across political divide Ms Bright said the ultimate test should be whether the Commission could earn the trust of both major political parties and the wider Ghanaian public, particularly when its decisions did not favour their interests. She stressed that improving the appointment process was necessary to establish an electoral body whose independence and impartiality would be accepted across the political divide. “The test for me is whether we are building an Electoral Commission that both parties and the wider public, Ghanaians, can trust when decisions go against them,” she said.

items.title: Prise en charge de l’infertilité : Une gynécologue appelle à briser le silence et les préjugés
items.description: Ce vendredi 16 octobre, à la clôture d’un atelier de deux jours à l’intention des journalistes en santé, le Dr Ndèye Khady Sène, gynécologue à l’hôpital régional de Kaolack, a souligné le poids des préjugés sociaux et le coût élevé des traitements liés à l’infertilité. Des défis qui, selon elle, compliquent fortement la prise en charge des patients. L’infertilité ne doit plus être considérée comme une affaire exclusivement féminine. C’est le principal message porté par la gynécologue Ndèye Khady Sène, le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, à l’issue de l’atelier de deux jours consacré à cette problématique et organisé par la Direction de la santé de la mère et de l’enfant (Dsme) en collaboration avec l’Association des journalistes en santé, population et développement (Ajspd). « L’infertilité concerne le couple et non uniquement la femme. Il faut donc rechercher les causes aussi bien chez la femme que chez l’homme », a-t-elle précisé. Dans la société sénégalaise, l’absence de grossesse est encore trop souvent imputée à l’épouse, exposant de nombreuses femmes aux accusations, aux pressions familiales et aux tensions conjugales. « Certaines finissent par s’isoler, par crainte du regard des autres. Il est urgent de déconstruire ces préjugés et de mieux faire connaître les différentes causes de l’infertilité », a préconisé la praticienne. D’après le Dr Sène, les difficultés à concevoir peuvent notamment être liées à des troubles de l’ovulation, à des lésions des trompes, à l’endométriose ou à des anomalies du sperme. D’où l’importance d'un bilan médical complet pour les deux partenaires. Elle a également mis en garde contre l’automédication, insistant sur la nécessité d'une consultation adaptée afin d'identifier l’origine du problème et de proposer un traitement adéquat. Au-delà des préjugés, le coût des soins constitue un obstacle majeur. Les examens, les médicaments et les techniques de Procréation médicalement assistée (Pma) représentent des dépenses considérables pour les ménages. « Il faut aussi un accompagnement émotionnel du couple et un effort financier », a expliqué la gynécologue, tout en rappelant que ces traitements « nécessitent des moyens et un suivi rigoureux, sans garantir systématiquement une grossesse ». À l’hôpital régional de Kaolack, des efforts sont déployés pour améliorer la prise en charge. Selon les chiffres présentés par le Dr Sène, 3720 patients ont consulté pour des problèmes d'infertilité entre 2021 et 2025. Le service a également réalisé 121 inséminations, avec un taux de grossesse de 25 % pour cette procédure. Un plaidoyer attendu des médias Le directeur de la Santé de la mère et de l’enfant, le Dr Amadou Doucouré, a souligné le rôle clé des journalistes dans la sensibilisation des populations et le plaidoyer en faveur d’une meilleure prise en charge de l’infertilité. Au-delà de la simple diffusion d’informations, les professionnels des médias sont appelés à mettre en lumière les difficultés rencontrées par les couples, particulièrement les femmes défavorisées face à l'accès aux soins. « Il s’agit aussi de faire évoluer les mentalités, de déconstruire les préjugés et de lutter contre la stigmatisation liée à l’infertilité », a-t-il affirmé. Le Dr Doucouré a, en outre, rappelé l’importance de documenter les insuffisances du dispositif actuel. « Les journalistes doivent montrer les avancées réalisées, mais aussi les difficultés persistantes et les aspects à améliorer, qu’il s’agisse de l’accès aux traitements, des moyens disponibles ou du renforcement des compétences techniques », a-t-il déclaré.Pour Eugène Kaly, président de l’Ajspd, c'est à travers des reportages de terrain et des campagnes de sensibilisation que les médias pourront interpeller les décideurs, contribuer à l’identification des besoins et favoriser l’émergence de réponses adaptées. « L’enjeu est de faire du traitement médiatique de l’infertilité un levier de changement social et d’amélioration de l’accès aux soins », a-t-il conclu. Babacar Guèye DIOP

items.title: Akosua Manu calls for a proper protection framework for sexually abused children
items.description: Adviser on Gender and Social Protection to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has called for a proper national child protection framework to safeguard pupils who suffer sexual abuse in schools. She said Ghana needs a clear system through which children can report abuse, receive protection and seek justice without fear of exposure or intimidation. Speaking on JoyNews ’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, during a discussion on sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Ms Manu said the current arrangements did not adequately protect children who reported such cases. “So, fundamentally, there’s no protection for these girls, for these children in the schools,” she said. She said that a national framework should establish safe and confidential reporting channels to ensure that children are protected and their concerns handled with the seriousness they deserve. “I would think to cure the problem, there should be a framework, a national protection framework, safeguarding these girls, where reports of such cases go to, that there should be a channel where you report to, where you get protected, where your name or where your form or whatever is hidden,” she said. Ms Manu said that the system must put the welfare of the child first, particularly when the alleged abuse involves someone in a position of authority within a school. “It should be such that the child is prioritised,” she added. Ms Manu also raised concerns about situations in which children are expected to report abuse to the same school authorities they accuse of misconduct. She said such arrangements could discourage victims from speaking out, especially when they fear that their complaints may not be handled fairly. “But I believe fundamentally a child should not have to seek justice from the same authorities that they’re accusing of abuse,” she said. Ms Manu referred to a News card shared by JoyNews which stated that six headteachers had allegedly sexually assaulted girls in their schools since 2025. She said the reported cases raised serious concerns about the effectiveness of existing measures to protect pupils and called for urgent policy action. “You can imagine the number of girls that have gone through this,” she said. “And you can imagine the ones that are under-reported. It is a national crisis,” she added, referring to the reported cases. The allegations against the Obuasi SHTS headmaster have not, in the details provided, been established as proven findings. Ms Manu’s call for reforms centres on ensuring that allegations of abuse are reported safely and investigated properly, while protecting children from further harm. She called for a policy that would make children feel comfortable reporting abuse and confident that their complaints would be handled appropriately. “We need to put a policy in place that makes kids comfortable,” she said. “The last place a child should not feel safe should not be a school. At least, at the very least, from home to school, they should feel safe,” she added.

items.title: Indian airlines barred from using Pakistani airspace until Nov 24 as ban extended
items.description: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban for Indian aircraft for another month, until Nov 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA). The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Oct 24. “Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said. According to the notice, the extension came into effect at 7:45pm on Saturday and will remain until 04:59am on Nov 24, 2026. The country’s airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) — Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022. Saturday’s Notam applies to both the Karachi (OPKR) and Lahore (OPLR) FIRs. India and Pakistan closed their airspaces to each other’s airlines in late April 2025, when tensions between them escalated in the wake of a deadly attack in India-occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam. On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass had announced a series of measures , including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country. New Delhi, without evidence, had alleged that Islamabad backed the Pahalgam attack. However, Pakistan had strongly denied any involvement and offered a neutral probe . The nuclear powers had the fiercest air battle in May, in which Pakistan said it downed seven Indian fighter jets. Since then, Pakistan has extended the airspace ban several times, forcing Indian carriers to use longer and costlier routes. For Air India, the country’s only carrier with a major international network, fuel costs rose by as much as 29 per cent and journey times by up to three hours on some long-haul routes, according to a document submitted to Indian officials last October. The airline, owned by Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, estimated the Pakistan airspace closure’s impact on its profit before tax at $455 million annually — a significant amount given its fiscal 2024-25 loss stood at $439m.

items.title: Looting, blazes and clashes in France amid nationwide protests
items.description: Police and protesters clashed violently in Paris and other French cities on Saturday on the sidelines of nationwide marches against soaring inflation, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off, multiple blazes set, and looters breaking into dozens of stores to strip them bare. With just months to go before the two-round elections in April and May to choose Macron’s successor, the demonstrations follow weeks of high-school student blockades demanding better learning conditions. Macron and his government were criticised by many of the demonstrators, who numbered 500,000 across the country, according to the CGT union. Authorities did not immediately give their estimate of the numbers. Police used tear gas and water cannon against masked protesters in Paris and other cities who were throwing projectiles and aiming fireworks. Several parked cars were torched in the capital, and more than 130 arrests were made. In the southern city of Saint-Etienne, a male protester had his hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, a police source told AFP . His maiming came after a 15-year-old lost his hand on October 5 to a police stun grenade during another protest in the city of Lens. Protesters stand amid tear gas smoke as clashes erupt ahead of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, at Place de la Republique in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP The protests geared up with a handful of gatherings nationwide on Saturday morning, AFP reporters said. In Lyon, protesters set ablaze a tourist office in the city centre, and smashed their way into town halls in the cities of Marseille and Lille, where they vandalised the premises before leaving. Dozens of shops were looted, including many in Marseille, among them a Hermes boutique, an Apple store in Lille, several shops in Nice and at least one mobile phone outlet in Paris, AFP journalists saw. A crowd of more than 300 protesters tried to move up Paris’s Champs-Elysees, home to flagship luxury stores. As police firing tear gas blocked their way, they yelled, “All cops are bastards”. In the western city of Rennes, around 20 people set up a barricade using trash bins and large pallets on the outskirts of a shopping mall. Christophe, a 47-year-old carpenter and former Yellow Vest protester who did not give his surname, said he was indignant after seeing what he viewed as police brutality against teenagers in recent weeks. “We’ve reached the point where the repression is targeting our own children,” he told AFP . A French national police officer fires tear gas during clashes prior to the start of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Marseille, southern France on October 17, 2026. — AFP ‘Macron, resign’ The looting and confrontations with police were being carried out by masked youths on the sidelines of marches that were largely peaceful and which attracted people of all ages, including families with children. Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire stressed that “the overwhelming majority of demonstrators” wanted to “march calmly”, but “acts of vandalism” were tarnishing their protest. In Paris, tens of thousands marched across the east and north of the city in one major march, some shouting “Everyone hates the police” and “Macron, resign”. Protesters wearing yellow vests face police as clashes erupt ahead of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, at Place de la Republique in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP One demonstrator, Jules Petrichor, 47, who had brought his son, said: “There was a good atmosphere and then suddenly they (the police) started gassing us, even though nothing was happening. Naturally that worsened things and the hot-heads got hot-headed.” Another protester who gave his first name as Louis, 19, complained that police were trigger-happy any time there was a demonstration. “We can’t protest any more, it’s frightening,” he said. The country’s Yellow Vest movement, which eight years ago staged street protests against Macron’s government over planned fuel tax hikes, has called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations. It has appealed to teachers and students, workers, pensioners and farmers to take part in the protests on the first day of half-term holidays. The principal grievance was the cost of living — pushed up in part by the war in the Middle East — that has helped send inflation soaring in Europe as elsewhere. But there were other issues too. A protestor with a gas mask holds a French flag in front of a fire at the Boulevard des Capucines during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP High school student Kamil Alahyan, 18, said he was protesting “for so many reasons — the elections coming up in 2027, politicians who lie, the ultra-rich who’ve been taking more and more wealth over the past 10 years”. “For years we’ve had climate, economy and equality problems but the government is not doing anything about it,” said Agnes, a 50-year-old actor who did not give her second name. Anae, a 24-year-old student who did not give her surname, said she was protesting because she did not have a “sustainable future”. “Our planet’s burning. And we’ve got a government that doesn’t give a toss,” she said. Le Pen blames ‘rioters’ Opposition politicians vying to succeed Macron have seized upon the protests. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who has sided with the police, said on X: “Looting, pillaging, attacking police — rioters have once again sullied the October 17 demonstrations over the cost of living.” She claimed that the protesters’ demands had been “hijacked by the far left”. Her far-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon, insisted early Saturday that “everything is passing off peacefully”, while accusing television news of “flooding us with images of violence in dozens of cities”. Several protesters sought to draw parallels with the French Revolution of 1789. “It’s the Revolution — we’re taking the Bastille!” some shouted in Marseille during the forced entry of the mayor’s offices. In the western city of La Rochelle, marchers streamed behind a placard reading: “Revolution or death.” And in the southern city of Montpellier, a giant blue sign reading “The people will win” was unfurled above a central square. “The government is trembling and it’s right to tremble because when the French people are angry, they never let up,” Ryad Rani, the head of the LSU high school student representative body, told journalists in Paris.

items.title: ‘Cockroach’ party founder released by Indian police
items.description: India’s youth-led Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after his arrest during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority. Dipke, 31, was detained Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital’s central Connaught Place district. items.title: Haaland double helps Manchester City win, Neto brace cheers Chelsea
items.description: Manchester City bounced back from their midweek setback in Europe to maintain their perfect Premier League start with Erling Haaland’s double propelling them to a 3-2 home win over Ipswich Town on Saturday. Paris Saint-Germain inflicted a first meaningful defeat on Enzo Maresca’s side in the Champions League on Wednesday but City shrugged off a gallant Ipswich side to make it seven wins from seven to cement their place at the top of the table. Chelsea beat Everton 2-0 in Saturday’s early action thanks to Pedro Neto’s brace although the London club’s win was overshadowed by an injury to goalkeeper Emi Martinez. Liverpool came from a goal down to beat Brentford 2-1 away although they were helped by the previously unbeaten hosts being reduced to 10 men shortly before halftime when Yehor Yarmolyuk was shown a straight red card for a head butt. Victory lifted Liverpool above Brentford into fifth place with 12 points behind Chelsea in fourth on 13. Fulham moved off the foot of the table with their first league win of the season — 1-0 at home to Hull City. Dark clouds remain over the Etihad Stadium with Manchester City’s fate still unknown after they appealed a ruling that the club breached 114 Premier League financial rules. City have always denied any wrongdoing. But on the pitch it is very much business as usual, especially for Norwegian goal machine Haaland. Phil Foden gave City a short-lived lead cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, but Haaland restored the home side’s advantage before halftime with a header from Mateo Kovacic’s cross. Haaland then gave his side some breathing space with his second in the 69th minute, powering past Ipswich’s Abdoul Ouattara before a low finish into the corner. He was denied a hat-trick by an offside decision and Ipswich got a lifeline when Zian Flemming tucked away a penalty in stoppage time but City bagged the points. Feisty first half Chelsea have had a knack of scoring early this season but were kept at bay by hosts Everton in a feisty and physical first half that produced five yellow cards. However, Xabi Alonso’s visitors needed just 43 seconds after the restart to go 1-0 up when Jorrel Hato cut the ball back from the byline to find Neto who swept home. Martinez’s clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite caused a lengthy stoppage with paramedics coming onto the pitch. The Argentina keeper was eventually strapped to a stretcher and taken off, leading to 11 minutes of stoppage time. Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez collides with Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite during their Premier League match at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool on October 17, 2026.— Reuters Chelsea doubled their lead in the 90th minute when Neto pounced on a loose ball after Jordan Henderson’s free kick was blocked by the wall, finding the bottom corner with a composed finish as Everton suffered their first defeat of the season. “What we know is he (Martinez) left the stadium conscious and right now he is in the hospital doing precautionary tests,” Alonso said. “It was concussion but more than that I saw only one clip. Hopefully it won’t be too bad but we need to wait.” Martinez’s knock gave 21-year-old keeper Mike Penders the chance to make his Premier League debut and he helped Chelsea keep a clean sheet in the league for the first time in 23 games. “We need a clean sheet, to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike did as well,” Alonso added. Liverpool deservedly fell behind at Brentford with Keane Lewis-Potter putting the hosts in front. Brentford were good value for their lead but Yarmolyuk’s rush of blood to the head when he clashed with Jeremy Jacquet at a Liverpool corner changed the game. After referee John Brooks was invited to check a VAR monitor he brandished the red card at Ukrainian Yarmolyuk who trudged off to applause from the home fans. Liverpool huffed and puffed after the break but Victor Munoz finally levelled in the 62nd minute when he cut in to beat keeper Caoimhin Kelleher with a left-foot finish. Liverpool’s Victor Munoz (R) shoots to score against Brentford during their Premier League match at the GTech Community Stadium in London on October 17, 2026.— Reuters Alexander Isak won it for Andoni Iraola’s side eight minutes later with a clinical strike from Bradley Barcola’s assist. Brentford ended with nine men after Vitaly Janelt got a second yellow card for a foul on substitute Rio Ngumoha. Elsewhere, Alex Iwobi’s 33rd-minute strike for Fulham was enough to earn their new manager Alvaro Arbeloa a long-overdue league win and move Fulham up to 15th.

items.description: TEHRAN- A deeper understanding of the relationship between religious institutions and the arts is essential to addressing longstanding challenges surrounding music in Iran, cultural sociologist Hossein Sarvi says, emphasizing the need for informed dialogue and a reassessment of institutional relations.

items.title: France : les grandes villes en proie aux pillages en marge des manifestations contre la "vie chère"
items.description: De Paris à Marseille, la journée de mobilisation contre la "vie chère" a réuni des centaines de milliers de personnes samedi mais s'est conclue par des affrontements et des scènes de chaos d'une intensité rare, des "casseurs" se livrant jusque dans la soirée à des pillages et dégradations vivement condamnés par l'exécutif.

items.title: Israelis beat Washington Post journalist in military-backed West Bank raids
items.description: TEHRAN — The men came down from a hilltop settlement shortly after 8 a.m. on Friday, dressed in black, carrying slingshots and batons. At least one had a gun. By the time they finished, olive groves around Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, were burning, villagers were bleeding, and an American photographer for The Washington Post lay on the ground being kicked.

items.title: Trump’s White House chaotically turns on itself as Republicans brace for defeat
items.description: TEHRAN — A press secretary hired on a Friday and gone the next. An ambassador’s ouster announced during her only briefing.
